...or this is just a casual oversight that happens sometimes.

posts.content_html_raw:
Let's get down to business now and discuss a few things I found noteworthy in this update:
First of all, I fear those scenes really gave me an adult woman fetish and I feel vile and disgusting now, yuck! Selebus is really pushing the boundaries with his controversial sexual escapades.

Apart from how hot Rika is, as others mentioned, it's quite funny how Akira keeps getting away with things by the virtue of having a giant penis as well as an inhumane blood flow and horse-like stamina. My man.
It should be clear however to both him and the player that it's just postponing the inevitable and he'll have to have a more serious talk with the two eventually.

For Rika I kind of get it why Sel finally addressed the issue of "why haven't they fucked yet", given that Akira and Rin are finally becoming a thing and I feel it would be awkward to have Akira start having sex with Rika after Rin. This way it's less of a betrayal, as confirmed by Rin herself, since she even suggested it a few updates ago.
It'll still be interesting to see though how Rika reacts when she is confronted with the fact that this monster shlong wielding deviant is banging over half the class, including her daughter by then I assume.
Will it end up like with Maki? Possible. But I feel Rika has a more chaotic and, ironically, open-minded view on the world it seems and I could see her coming to terms with it at some point, depending how the whole story develops.

Imani for me is still the most problematic kind of character here though, because unlike Maki or Rika, she doesn't have a daughter that is in love with the predator that complicates the whole situation, she herself is in love with him.
A revelation of this magnitude should make her be able to view it as what it is and I find it more difficult to imagine an argument that would convince her to continue her adoration for this man. Maki and Rika have their relationship with their daughters to lose when threatening real consequences, Imani does not, unless you count her student-teacher relationships. Which, technically, should be only professional in the first place. She could rather easily just say "well fuck that, I didn't know you're like that, I will change schools and not have any contact with you anymore". Now I figure this is not the direction it will go, but I'm curious to see how Sel will make her wrap her mind around it and not lose said mind in the process.

Few words to the Maki situation as well, I believe this has been discussed thoroughly already but I do kind of understand her as well and feel mostly bad for her rather than be mad at her being a bad mother, which yeah, she has been for a while already, if not kinda always. But this story shines through the imperfections and failures of characters, in my opinion, so I don't actually mind it and even like when a character which I have been mostly bored with so far actually shows emotion and provides some drama, for understandable reasons, only to be shattered with the realization that she is pretty much all alone with her take and crumbling down from the pressure. In a way, she is the most sane person right now but surrounded by delusional and conflicted people who won't listen to her.
Speaking of reasonable people, Osako. I've grown to like Osako. She is insecure but kind, she wants to help people but ultimately she has to help herself first. Very relatable.
This update was huge for her. The whole Ayane scene felt so good. This fated accumulation of circumstances, with Osako giving her sunflowers and Ayane subconsciously giving her this aura of a mother missing her child. They really helped each other find what they need right now. It was very cute and felt just right.
Consequently, the next scene was even more bittersweet as a result. I felt bad for Wakana, but at the end of the day, it seems what Ayane alluded might be true. Maybe they just don't want the same things in life. And it's a sign of real character growth that Osako realizes that in the last moment and steps up before it's too late.

Very interesting dynamic and I'm curious to see where it leads to.
Story-wise it obviously opens the door for Akira getting his opportunity to be a rebound for both eventually, in their phase of trying to find themselves. Somehow Sel has to make Osako and Wakane sex (with Akira that is) happen naturally, and it would kind of feel cheap if a married Osako and Wakana agreed to a threesome like this just willy-nilly.
As I mentioned in a previous post, I'm on the red path and avoided Stomachache just because I didn't want to get through a scene watching Io be miserable - I like her. But life is life and all, also I would be missing a scene, so I went through it now and switched over to her green path to get her full experience for this update.

It was luckily worth it. Not (entirely) because it was hot and really sweet in itself, but because of what it meant for her as a character - growth. Not even solely sexually in my opinion, but just as a sign that the trauma she had to endure is not going to have chokehold on her entire life, that she can do things despite the trauma and overcome it partially with the help of others.

However, I was surprised that seemingly nobody discussed the fact that this development only occurs if Stomacheache happened.
At first, I found it a little counterintuitive. Wouldn't it be more likely that a happy and cheerful Io who finally learned to trust the person she is in love with, have that person help her explore her sexuality step by step? And the Io that was, once again, disappointed and used by another adult be more reluctant to openly suggest doing more sexual activities? Even mentioning that she masturbates, despite giving the impression that she would never do that during Stomachache?

I thought about it for a while and for now I'm more on Sel's side now. I guess an Io that saw that Akira is happy with her the way she is, not needing to stoop so low as to basically force her to be sexually active with him, wouldn't really have an incentive to go further down that line. What for? She already has what she wants and it didn't need to involve sex.
The Stomachache Io however basically learnt that Akira, for whichever reason it may ultimately be, has this need to be sexual with her. And while she doesn't like doing it any more than the other Io, she understands that she has to make some compromises in order to satisfy him, knowing that he does not intend to do any harm.

I think both versions go through some personal growth here, as someone already mentioned, Red path Io learns that she can in fact trust another adult and just be herself and still be loved. While Green path Io learns that she can try to overcome her trauma for someone she loves and be vulnerable.
Either way, she essentially fights her trust issues and hopefully also eventually her immense insecurity and self-worth issues.

Knowing this however, I wonder how much the story will ultimately change for her in those two versions though? With this update I feel like it will be mostly a question of missing lewd events with her for the red path and some flavor text changes like it has been so far. But that it will lead to the same conclusion, I guess.

Correct me if I'm wrong though: Sel confirmed that all main and side characters will have sex scenes before the purity routes. Does anyone know if that only applies to the green path?
I assume so, since it would be kind of fucked up for Akira to end up still having sex with red path Io after all this. And maybe even more so with Ami, given that on red path he stubbornly rejected her advances throughout the game. And even more so with the wizards, obviously.
Maybe that's the whole point of the green path leading to the only true ending though. They already somehow got to the point where they willingly have sex with Akira, instead of potentially having to force it on the red path when it comes to the end of the game.

Also, regarding her sinkhole experience, what was the name of that god she encounter again? I know he was also present in the karaoke box, at the ramen shop and with Kaori previously. Also seems to be closely connected to Nao. What's his role/significance? Can someone sum it up or interpret his appearance?
Rin is great. Rin is a true homie. I get that some might find her behavior excessively mean and out of character in this update, but I feel her. She needed that. And Chika needed it too, to some extent. She did it the hard way, but it'll ultimately make things easier for Chika to get back to normal eventually.

Speaking of which, I really like her new old look. Also damn, Chika insulting Ami in Tagalog is both the funniest and sexiest thing I have seen her do since she wore that dog costume and it immediately catapulted her to a higher rank for me. The comeback is on, boys!

Regarding Rin's TSS, I felt like Onund's mention of "another you" was significant. There have been many theories over the years that Rin and Sana are sisters, both children of Nozomu or even Akira. Now Onund specifcally says her birth mother left her for a smaller you. That does imply it would be someone younger, which then makes it unlikely to be any of our main cast since it's established that Rin is the youngest, I believe.
I feel like it will still become relevant though. The fact that so many character's fathers have remained a mystery yet must have some significance to the story. Sel does not shy away from essentially writing them off as irrelevant if they do exist, like with Futaba or Makoto, so I assume them being unknown is of importance.

Who or what the eyeless Rin represents though, beats me. Could be some sort of result of different timelines going wrong but who knows. I assume all of these different dimension thingies will only make sense much later in the game.
Despite how I ranked it in my earlier meme, the Touka scene was obviously the hottest one this update. What a smoke show she is, holy mother of Akira Christ.
Normally I would get really mad after such an intense display of blue balling, but I feel like Touka deserves another proper shot at her first time with Akira. Props to her though for being so assertive and knowing what she wants.

That whole talk about Tsubasa was very interesting as well though. She is really catching on and I think she is on to something. Tsubasa clearly wants her daughters to have sex with Akira. But why? Touka knows her mother well enough to understand that she is conflicted about this, that she wouldn't want this unless there was a really good reason for it.
And I think the reason might be HOPE.
As other already concluded, it almost has to be assumed that she is somehow in on this whole thing, with what Yasu says and HOPE in a more direct manner, that the girls need to find the light by, essentially, Akira's holy "saber".

But what does Tsubasa know exactly that makes her so convinced that it needs to happen? She must have seen something, lived another timeline, been visited by another version of herself or someone she knows who told her the importance of it happening.
I don't get why else she would be so pressed on her daughters, and herself apparently, getting it on with Akira, when she is clearly also upset about it. The whole thing with the arranged marriage at least is definitely bogus, or only a cover story to give an out for this to be initiated with Tsukasa, which would be obviously the hardest part.

spoilers.title: Io
spoilers.html:
As I mentioned in a previous post, I'm on the red path and avoided Stomachache just because I didn't want to get through a scene watching Io be miserable - I like her. But life is life and all, also I would be missing a scene, so I went through it now and switched over to her green path to get her full experience for this update.

It was luckily worth it. Not (entirely) because it was hot and really sweet in itself, but because of what it meant for her as a character - growth. Not even solely sexually in my opinion, but just as a sign that the trauma she had to endure is not going to have chokehold on her entire life, that she can do things despite the trauma and overcome it partially with the help of others.

However, I was surprised that seemingly nobody discussed the fact that this development only occurs if Stomacheache happened.
At first, I found it a little counterintuitive. Wouldn't it be more likely that a happy and cheerful Io who finally learned to trust the person she is in love with, have that person help her explore her sexuality step by step? And the Io that was, once again, disappointed and used by another adult be more reluctant to openly suggest doing more sexual activities? Even mentioning that she masturbates, despite giving the impression that she would never do that during Stomachache?

I thought about it for a while and for now I'm more on Sel's side now. I guess an Io that saw that Akira is happy with her the way she is, not needing to stoop so low as to basically force her to be sexually active with him, wouldn't really have an incentive to go further down that line. What for? She already has what she wants and it didn't need to involve sex.
The Stomachache Io however basically learnt that Akira, for whichever reason it may ultimately be, has this need to be sexual with her. And while she doesn't like doing it any more than the other Io, she understands that she has to make some compromises in order to satisfy him, knowing that he does not intend to do any harm.

I think both versions go through some personal growth here, as someone already mentioned, Red path Io learns that she can in fact trust another adult and just be herself and still be loved. While Green path Io learns that she can try to overcome her trauma for someone she loves and be vulnerable.
Either way, she essentially fights her trust issues and hopefully also eventually her immense insecurity and self-worth issues.

Knowing this however, I wonder how much the story will ultimately change for her in those two versions though? With this update I feel like it will be mostly a question of missing lewd events with her for the red path and some flavor text changes like it has been so far. But that it will lead to the same conclusion, I guess.

Correct me if I'm wrong though: Sel confirmed that all main and side characters will have sex scenes before the purity routes. Does anyone know if that only applies to the green path?
I assume so, since it would be kind of fucked up for Akira to end up still having sex with red path Io after all this. And maybe even more so with Ami, given that on red path he stubbornly rejected her advances throughout the game. And even more so with the wizards, obviously.
Maybe that's the whole point of the green path leading to the only true ending though. They already somehow got to the point where they willingly have sex with Akira, instead of potentially having to force it on the red path when it comes to the end of the game.

Also, regarding her sinkhole experience, what was the name of that god she encounter again? I know he was also present in the karaoke box, at the ramen shop and with Kaori previously. Also seems to be closely connected to Nao. What's his role/significance? Can someone sum it up or interpret his appearance?

spoilers.title: Rin
spoilers.html:
Rin is great. Rin is a true homie. I get that some might find her behavior excessively mean and out of character in this update, but I feel her. She needed that. And Chika needed it too, to some extent. She did it the hard way, but it'll ultimately make things easier for Chika to get back to normal eventually.

Speaking of which, I really like her new old look. Also damn, Chika insulting Ami in Tagalog is both the funniest and sexiest thing I have seen her do since she wore that dog costume and it immediately catapulted her to a higher rank for me. The comeback is on, boys!

Regarding Rin's TSS, I felt like Onund's mention of "another you" was significant. There have been many theories over the years that Rin and Sana are sisters, both children of Nozomu or even Akira. Now Onund specifcally says her birth mother left her for a smaller you. That does imply it would be someone younger, which then makes it unlikely to be any of our main cast since it's established that Rin is the youngest, I believe.
I feel like it will still become relevant though. The fact that so many character's fathers have remained a mystery yet must have some significance to the story. Sel does not shy away from essentially writing them off as irrelevant if they do exist, like with Futaba or Makoto, so I assume them being unknown is of importance.

Who or what the eyeless Rin represents though, beats me. Could be some sort of result of different timelines going wrong but who knows. I assume all of these different dimension thingies will only make sense much later in the game.

spoilers.title: Touka
spoilers.html:
Despite how I ranked it in my earlier meme, the Touka scene was obviously the hottest one this update. What a smoke show she is, holy mother of Akira Christ.
Normally I would get really mad after such an intense display of blue balling, but I feel like Touka deserves another proper shot at her first time with Akira. Props to her though for being so assertive and knowing what she wants.

That whole talk about Tsubasa was very interesting as well though. She is really catching on and I think she is on to something. Tsubasa clearly wants her daughters to have sex with Akira. But why? Touka knows her mother well enough to understand that she is conflicted about this, that she wouldn't want this unless there was a really good reason for it.
And I think the reason might be HOPE.
As other already concluded, it almost has to be assumed that she is somehow in on this whole thing, with what Yasu says and HOPE in a more direct manner, that the girls need to find the light by, essentially, Akira's holy "saber".

But what does Tsubasa know exactly that makes her so convinced that it needs to happen? She must have seen something, lived another timeline, been visited by another version of herself or someone she knows who told her the importance of it happening.
I don't get why else she would be so pressed on her daughters, and herself apparently, getting it on with Akira, when she is clearly also upset about it. The whole thing with the arranged marriage at least is definitely bogus, or only a cover story to give an out for this to be initiated with Tsukasa, which would be obviously the hardest part.

However, I was surprised that seemingly nobody discussed the fact that this development only occurs if Stomacheache happened.
At first, I found it a little counterintuitive. Wouldn't it be more likely that a happy and cheerful Io who finally learned to trust the person she is in love with, have that person help her explore her sexuality step by step? And the Io that was, once again, disappointed and used by another adult be more reluctant to openly suggest doing more sexual activities? Even mentioning that she masturbates, despite giving the impression that she would never do that during Stomachache?

I thought about it for a while and for now I'm more on Sel's side now. I guess an Io that saw that Akira is happy with her the way she is, not needing to stoop so low as to basically force her to be sexually active with him, wouldn't really have an incentive to go further down that line. What for? She already has what she wants and it didn't need to involve sex.
The Stomachache Io however basically learnt that Akira, for whichever reason it may ultimately be, has this need to be sexual with her. And while she doesn't like doing it any more than the other Io, she understands that she has to make some compromises in order to satisfy him, knowing that he does not intend to do any harm.

I think both versions go through some personal growth here, as someone already mentioned, Red path Io learns that she can in fact trust another adult and just be herself and still be loved. While Green path Io learns that she can try to overcome her trauma for someone she loves and be vulnerable.
Either way, she essentially fights her trust issues and hopefully also eventually her immense insecurity and self-worth issues.

Knowing this however, I wonder how much the story will ultimately change for her in those two versions though? With this update I feel like it will be mostly a question of missing lewd events with her for the red path and some flavor text changes like it has been so far. But that it will lead to the same conclusion, I guess.

Correct me if I'm wrong though: Sel confirmed that all main and side characters will have sex scenes before the purity routes. Does anyone know if that only applies to the green path?
I assume so, since it would be kind of fucked up for Akira to end up still having sex with red path Io after all this. And maybe even more so with Ami, given that on red path he stubbornly rejected her advances throughout the game. And even more so with the wizards, obviously.
Maybe that's the whole point of the green path leading to the only true ending though. They already somehow got to the point where they willingly have sex with Akira, instead of potentially having to force it on the red path when it comes to the end of the game.

Also seems to be closely connected to Nao. What's his role/significance? Can someone sum it up or interpret his appearance?

spoilers.title: Rin
spoilers.html:
Rin is great. Rin is a true homie. I get that some might find her behavior excessively mean and out of character in this update, but I feel her. She needed that. And Chika needed it too, to some extent. She did it the hard way, but it'll ultimately make things easier for Chika to get back to normal eventually.

Speaking of which, I really like her new old look. Also damn, Chika insulting Ami in Tagalog is both the funniest and sexiest thing I have seen her do since she wore that dog costume and it immediately catapulted her to a higher rank for me. The comeback is on, boys!

Regarding Rin's TSS, I felt like Onund's mention of "another you" was significant. There have been many theories over the years that Rin and Sana are sisters, both children of Nozomu or even Akira. Now Onund specifcally says her birth mother left her for a smaller you. That does imply it would be someone younger, which then makes it unlikely to be any of our main cast since it's established that Rin is the youngest, I believe.
I feel like it will still become relevant though. The fact that so many character's fathers have remained a mystery yet must have some significance to the story. Sel does not shy away from essentially writing them off as irrelevant if they do exist, like with Futaba or Makoto, so I assume them being unknown is of importance.

Who or what the eyeless Rin represents though, beats me. Could be some sort of result of different timelines going wrong but who knows. I assume all of these different dimension thingies will only make sense much later in the game.

spoilers.title: Touka
spoilers.html:
Despite how I ranked it in my earlier meme, the Touka scene was obviously the hottest one this update. What a smoke show she is, holy mother of Akira Christ.
Normally I would get really mad after such an intense display of blue balling, but I feel like Touka deserves another proper shot at her first time with Akira. Props to her though for being so assertive and knowing what she wants.

That whole talk about Tsubasa was very interesting as well though. She is really catching on and I think she is on to something. Tsubasa clearly wants her daughters to have sex with Akira. But why? Touka knows her mother well enough to understand that she is conflicted about this, that she wouldn't want this unless there was a really good reason for it.
And I think the reason might be HOPE.
As other already concluded, it almost has to be assumed that she is somehow in on this whole thing, with what Yasu says and HOPE in a more direct manner, that the girls need to find the light by, essentially, Akira's holy "saber".

But what does Tsubasa know exactly that makes her so convinced that it needs to happen? She must have seen something, lived another timeline, been visited by another version of herself or someone she knows who told her the importance of it happening.
I don't get why else she would be so pressed on her daughters, and herself apparently, getting it on with Akira, when she is clearly also upset about it. The whole thing with the arranged marriage at least is definitely bogus, or only a cover story to give an out for this to be initiated with Tsukasa, which would be obviously the hardest part.

spoilers.title: Io
spoilers.html:
That was me, I was the one that talked about the different versions of Io for red path, and green path.

I've sat through both versions of her story now, and still maintain that red path is the 'morally' correct path for her. Green path is simply Io being groomed by another adult. Was it super adorable how happy she was kissing Akira while jerking him off? Yeah, absolutely...but the price she is paying isn't actually helping her. It's simply her falling into a new role of sexual abuse. Can she grow from it? Sure! Is she choosing to participate? Sure! But Io says it herself...if she had known the kind of person Akira was, she NEVER would have fallen for him. She would have stayed the fuck away from him...

But of course, Akira is the Greatest Groomer To Ever Groom, so Io fell under his spell before realizing the type of person he is.

Red path, though, is letting Akira AND Io grow as people. It's healing...Io is such a complex character, and an absolute doll. She deserves an adult to love, that she doesn't need to perform for like a fucking circus monkey. She shouldn't need to think that the only way Akira will love her is if she performs for him...

Imagine how terrible her abuse was, that when an adult turns down the opportunity to fuck her...she asks them if they are an Angel. That's intense, and exactly what she deserves, if we consider what makes each of the girls happy. If the ultimate goal of the game is to give everyone a happy ending, her happy ending is being loved for who she is, by the man she has fallen for and trusts, without having to deal with sex at all.

spoilers.title: Touka
spoilers.html:
There was that scene where Tsubasa meets with Himawari, and says she knows what she is; She even mentions that she has had dealings with their kind in the past. We currently don't have anymore information on that, but it's certainly a part of why she is dealing with Akira the way she is. She doesn't seem to recognize Himawari, so it had to be someone else. Could be Shiori, seeing as she wipes her own memory after every job...but it could also just be as simple as her thinking that Himawari is a god of some sort, and has had experience with other gods in the past.

I could probably theorize all day as to WHY she wants Akira to sleep with her daughters...but I kinda think the obvious answer is that she loves them, and wants them to survive the coming "True" end of the world.

Point 1: The Family library - Has books that detail the religion that Yasu follows. Has enough details that Touka was able to put things together that Yasu isn't full crazy...and I'm 100% certain that Tsubasa would have read those books as well.

Point 2: Touka and Tsubasa are well aware that Yasu absolutely knows the future, and other things she couldn't possibly know about; If that's the case, and Yasu of course claims that all of that knowledge comes from the God of her religion...then maybe there is more to said religion. As they say about the supernatural and paranormal...it's impossible to truly believe until you experience it yourself. Even if you're not religious, how hard would it be to continue to not believe if you've got a small white haired girl spouting off future knowledge, and things she has no way to know about...and claims her GOD tells her those things? Would definitely require atleast a second look...

Point 3: What is one of the seemingly most important parts of Yasu's religion? That Akira is important to it, and that being "saved"(Yasu's words), requires Energy Transference from Akira. Yasu even says in the most recent update that Touka is her best friend, so of course she wants her saved the most...but what does saved mean in this context? Yasu has 100% gone on an 'end of the world' rant a few times, so I assume it's that. What that means, I dunno, but I imagine we'll find out.

If the only way for your children to survive the coming apocalypse was to sleep with Akira...are you going to help make that happen or nah?

I think if we take all of the things we know about Tsubasa(She knows about Himawari, She knows about Gods(Maybe), she definitely knows Akira is 'Important', She is frequently near Yasu, The family library has extremely old rare books about Yasu's God), I'd say that this is a fairly obvious reason for her to push both of her daughters towards Akira.

I went back and replayed the event where Maki finds out that Akira was sexually abused, and she reiterates again how she "lost her virginity so late in life", so there's another hole in the Maki-in-the-video theory. That said, there's always the possibility that she's been lying about that the whole time and hiding it out of shame. At this point in the story, she's clearly into Akira and doesn't know him well enough to know that he wouldn't judge her for that, so that explanation smoothes that over. Also, upon replay of Maki's accusation of Akira at his home, when she mentions how these girls are at the most vulnerable time of their lives, Maki does seem to talk as if she's coming from personal experience. Most importantly, during Makoto's blowout at Maki, when Maki breaks down and is crying, she explicitly says, "I don't want you...to be like me..." It begs the question then, why not say that out loud to Akira when she's accusing him of misconduct? You could reasonably argue that Maki was interrupted by Makoto and Miku before dropping the final bombshell, or maybe she was keeping it in reserve since Akira could quip back, "Well I think you turned out perfectly fine..." I dunno, the theory is convincing, but just not convincing enough for me to fully commit to. I'll demote it from "nearly official canon" to "personal headcanon that I like."

On the topic of Makoto's confrontation with Maki, I might be speaking out of my biases since Maki and Makoto are some of my favorite characters, but Makoto's confrontation with Maki is my personal favorite confrontation scene so far. What makes it so great for me is that both of these characters are making what are quite frankly reasonable choices from their frame of reference. Now before you tell me that what Maki did was insanely creepy and unhinged (and it absolutely is from our outside perspective), stop viewing the story from a third person perspective and zoom in on Maki's perspective—not as a person but as a character in the story:

>Your daughter is incredibly loyal to her teacher
>Spends loads of time with him, even outside of school and even outside of when he's a teacher
>The rest of his class are openly into him
>Your friends start fucking him, too
>One day find condoms out of the blue in your daughter's room
>One day your friends suddenly shift positions on adult/minor relations and look at you like you're crazy to disagree
>When mentioning how weird it is to your daughter, she immediately cuts to personal attacks that, while correct, don't effectively disprove your statements
>Remember that the same teacher mentioned being made into a monster by his abuser and looked guilty as fuck when he was saying it

Honestly, if I was in Maki's position, knowing what she did and having on hand an unethically produced tape that by all rights should be outlawed as CSAM with extensive knowledge about how damaging it was to the lives of the actresses, plus the added bonus of the main actress looking like my daughter, I'm not ashamed to admit that I probably would have done exactly what Maki did, especially knowing how hard it is to get a person like Akira to talk and knowing that he's incredibly guilt-driven. Skipping the talk and leaping straight into showing him how fucked up this is would be what I would do, and we can all see by the look on Akira's face when he started to stutter out his near-confession that it almost worked.

From Makoto's perspective, her reaction also makes perfect sense for her from her frame of reference. Now I may be self-inserting a bit since I was also a mouthy little shit when I was her age, but if I was a teenager with an unhealthy self-esteem and sexual outlook that I could reasonably pin on my mother (and I do, for different reasons—don't ask), just to walk in on that same woman having recently turned a 180 and clearly accusing my secret lover with a porno starring a person that looked almost exactly like me, I would have blown up in the same way that Makoto did, and I would have pulled out every personal attack I could just like Makoto did.

Watching their confrontation felt less like boxers trading blows like with most of the confrontations with Akira and more like watching a train-wreck in slow motion, like this moment was set on its rails and set into motion long ago and destined to happen, especially when both Maki and Makoto made their choices to pump the brakes and ease up on how aggressive they're being in the moment. For Maki, it was seeing Makoto's face when another blow was dealt to her self esteem and she responded accordingly. You can see the moment Maki's thinking "oh shit." For Makoto, it was seeing her mother cry for only the second time (as far as we're aware), rivaling in emotional intensity to the only other time she's ever cried in front of her, when her husband and father to her daughter fucking died. You can especially see it on Makoto's face the moment Maki starts wailing for Masahiro. This event when I saw two of my favorite characters both vent out their frustrations and both realize in real time that they've gone too far is just *chef's kiss.*

." For Makoto, it was seeing her mother cry for only the second time (as far as we're aware), rivaling in emotional intensity to the only other time she's ever cried in front of her,

spoilers.title: Counterpoint to Maki-In-The-Video Theory
spoilers.html: I went back and replayed the event where Maki finds out that Akira was sexually abused, and she reiterates again how she "lost her virginity so late in life", so there's another hole in the Maki-in-the-video theory. That said, there's always the possibility that she's been lying about that the whole time and hiding it out of shame. At this point in the story, she's clearly into Akira and doesn't know him well enough to know that he wouldn't judge her for that, so that explanation smoothes that over. Also, upon replay of Maki's accusation of Akira at his home, when she mentions how these girls are at the most vulnerable time of their lives, Maki does seem to talk as if she's coming from personal experience. Most importantly, during Makoto's blowout at Maki, when Maki breaks down and is crying, she explicitly says, "I don't want you...to be like me..." It begs the question then, why not say that out loud to Akira when she's accusing him of misconduct? You could reasonably argue that Maki was interrupted by Makoto and Miku before dropping the final bombshell, or maybe she was keeping it in reserve since Akira could quip back, "Well I think you turned out perfectly fine..." I dunno, the theory is convincing, but just not convincing enough for me to fully commit to. I'll demote it from "nearly official canon" to "personal headcanon that I like."

spoilers.html:
On the topic of Makoto's confrontation with Maki, I might be speaking out of my biases since Maki and Makoto are some of my favorite characters, but Makoto's confrontation with Maki is my personal favorite confrontation scene so far. What makes it so great for me is that both of these characters are making what are quite frankly reasonable choices from their frame of reference. Now before you tell me that what Maki did was insanely creepy and unhinged (and it absolutely is from our outside perspective), stop viewing the story from a third person perspective and zoom in on Maki's perspective—not as a person but as a character in the story:

>Your daughter is incredibly loyal to her teacher
>Spends loads of time with him, even outside of school and even outside of when he's a teacher
>The rest of his class are openly into him
>Your friends start fucking him, too
>One day find condoms out of the blue in your daughter's room
>One day your friends suddenly shift positions on adult/minor relations and look at you like you're crazy to disagree
>When mentioning how weird it is to your daughter, she immediately cuts to personal attacks that, while correct, don't effectively disprove your statements
>Remember that the same teacher mentioned being made into a monster by his abuser and looked guilty as fuck when he was saying it

Honestly, if I was in Maki's position, knowing what she did and having on hand an unethically produced tape that by all rights should be outlawed as CSAM with extensive knowledge about how damaging it was to the lives of the actresses, plus the added bonus of the main actress looking like my daughter, I'm not ashamed to admit that I probably would have done exactly what Maki did, especially knowing how hard it is to get a person like Akira to talk and knowing that he's incredibly guilt-driven. Skipping the talk and leaping straight into showing him how fucked up this is would be what I would do, and we can all see by the look on Akira's face when he started to stutter out his near-confession that it almost worked.

From Makoto's perspective, her reaction also makes perfect sense for her from her frame of reference. Now I may be self-inserting a bit since I was also a mouthy little shit when I was her age, but if I was a teenager with an unhealthy self-esteem and sexual outlook that I could reasonably pin on my mother (and I do, for different reasons—don't ask), just to walk in on that same woman having recently turned a 180 and clearly accusing my secret lover with a porno starring a person that looked almost exactly like me, I would have blown up in the same way that Makoto did, and I would have pulled out every personal attack I could just like Makoto did.

You can especially see it on Makoto's face the moment Maki starts wailing for Masahiro. This event when I saw two of my favorite characters both vent out their frustrations and both realize in real time that they've gone too far is just *chef's kiss.*

I think you made good points, I'll just add to them again. I had said way prior to this that Io wanted to be "whole". And I feel like this is one thing people can get wrong about her at first glance: Io is not assexual. Io is a sexual person that was traumatized by sexual assault. These are very different things.

What the latest event confirms (but was in fact already said) is that she does, in fact, have a sexual life/desire (with or without Akira). So I hope that we can put to rest the notion that "Io could go her life without needing to force herself to be sexual if not for Akira" cause that was never the case. And, in fact, again she reinforces that she was the one that sprung up "Stomachache" on him - despite what many still insist on.

I say this because there is a discussion to be had, but it is not one regarding Io's sexuality or lack there of. The discussion is about helping her in taking control of that part of her life back, or helping her be happy without that part of her life. This is the difference. Mind you, she wants to take her sexuality back. Thus, it is the difference between confrontation and avoidance.

Now, obviously "Stomachache" wouldn't ever be the ideal start for the confrontation path, they both agree on that and wouldn't ever want to repeat it. But we're talking about Akira and Io - nothing about them would ever be ideal. To where it led though is quite ideal (given the possibilities). Having Io lead the sexual encounters, be the one touching Akira, get her kisses - this is healing. She had entire parts of her being taken and ruined for her by her mother, and she is now taking control back, that is quite powerful and in service of herself, not Akira.

The question Selebus poses, I think, is kind of dumb though. In which route would she be happier? Well, none? Because both involve Akira. If we were talking just the path of life both are equally valid. Some sexual assault victims will take back their sexuality, and that's beautiful. And others will choose to forego it entirely, and while not "disney movie" ending, it is quite realistic and ultimately valid.

The question is dumb because we lack context. If Io has a happy ending, which she does via purity route, then it is irrelevant, as she'll be the happiest on it regardless. If we were to talk about she waking up one day out of 23 and having her experiences on it helping her, I think either is valid as well? Mostly she'd be pretty freaked out about Maya's world rather than a lunatic either letting her lead sexual encounters, or being okay with just kissing her instead (when he's already banging other 25 girls on the side).
The problem with the entire situation is that Akira ruins the entire thing cause the right answer will always be: don't get involved with this dude if Io had a responsible partner either path could work. Alas, she has Selebus. And Selebus is an ass.

It shows that this story is not an isekai story like the beginning has you believe, but that he is indeed who other characters are saying he is, and not just some nameless self-insert. Changing his name as you want defeats the point of the narrative, and is much like just crossing out names in a novel as I said before.

Dateline: Kumon-mi, Time and Date unknown, as the concept of both seem rather "fluid" around here.

Our first encounter was with a woman identified only as "Rika". We're pretty sure she was telling us there was some bad stuff going on, although to be honest, we barely understood anything she was saying. We did, however manage to get a lead on the next person to talk to, a woman named "Maki" at what Rika described as the shop that sells "pokey sex stuff".

Maki did appear much more certain about what was happening, along with being much easier to understand. She described gaslighting from everyone else she tried to go to and believed she was the only one who could actually see what was going on. However, she also couldn't resist trying to sell us something she called the "Penetrator 2000". She did apologize, saying that she can never get totally out of salesperson mode.

After many equally bizarre encounters with the locals, we eventually got to the hotbed of depravity at the center of it all: Kumon-mi High School. The psychological damage wrought by this monster was immense, with various people spouting nonsense about made-up holidays like "Christmalloween" and experiencing the same school year over and over with no one actually aging or changing grades. The students themselves showed signs of extreme emotional trauma, including:
  • One student wearing a dog collar and appearing to mimic the actual symptoms of rabies, even going so far as requiring her younger sister to wear a dog mask when out in public.
  • One student spouting religious propaganda and declaring that the female students need to receive "His Light" in order to protect themselves from some unidentified calamity.
  • One student describing the teacher as the "Herald of the Adolescents", but providing little useful information, as her dialogue consisted most of "weebnotes" containing trivia about various anime series and obscure facts about Japanese culture.
  • One student begging our reporter to bring her into a dark alley and "have his way with her". Just mentioning this seemed to send her into a frenzy of ecstasy, and she was unable to speak anymore after that.
  • One student claiming to have had her vagina literally "broken".
  • One student, on her first encounter with our reporter, simply lifting her skirt to show her underwear.
These are only some of the horror stories we encountered. Reports are that prior to his dismissal from the local high school, this teacher had essentially given up on actually teaching, mostly allowing students to do whatever they wanted while he slept in the classroom. Rumors about activities happening on (or even with) his office desk abound.

Why this madness was not stopped much earlier, especially given that it was essentially common knowledge, is unknown. Local theories range from actual divine intervention to "Sensei's magical penis". Apparently no one was immune to this madness.

In the end, our investigative reporter barely escaped with his life after encountering a red-haired girl later identified as the perp's niece.

posts.content_html_raw:
Well, it depends on where you're from. You don't need to be rich to have a thing for guns here in the US.
That being said, to not have means to kill other people is a very new thing in human society. Do you know for how long the concept of "police" has been around? Just about 300 years. We've been a society for 12 thousand.

Having guns, which basically are magic wands of death, is the closest we can get to being able to take ownership of our own justice (at least potentially). So if someone tries to harm you, you just kill them, instead of trying to call 911 and having the police find your corpse 12 hours later (if they even come).

For the Amamiyas specifically it is an incredible power move for a couple of different reasons. One is that Japan's military was banned under international law for having sided with the Nazis during WW2 (something we tend to gloss over). So, for a Japanese person to hold firearms, and specifically higher caliber firearms is a very big deal.

That being said, to not have means to kill other people is a very new thing in human society. Do you know for how long the concept of "police" has been around? Just about 300 years. We've been a society for 12 thousand.
Having guns, which basically are magic wands of death, is the closest we can get to being able to take ownership of our own justice (at least potentially). So if someone tries to harm you, you just kill them, instead of trying to call 911 and having the police find your corpse 12 hours later (if they even come).
For the Amamiyas specifically it is an incredible power move for a couple of different reasons. One is that Japan's military was banned under international law for having sided with the Nazis during WW2 (something we tend to gloss over). So, for a Japanese person to hold firearms, and speficially higher caliber firearms is a very big deal.
Secondly, it is, to a lesser extent, stating that you aren't that Japanese, to be honest. Japanese people tend to be very much non-confrontational, and open-carrying firearms in the streets of a country that both can't do that, and is very much against anyone calling attention to themselves, is saying that you're above normality (which is a big thing for rich people). Obviously, this has a lot to do with Selebus being an American from Texas, much more than anything to do with his "Japanese" characters, when they're all actually American characters with a "Japanese" coating when it suits him.

Well, after ~260 hours i finally finished the latest update and now have free time for other stuff.
Praise be.
I have a bunch of thoughs and questions, which over the course of 3100+ pages were probably answered, but eh.
Very interesting plot developments regarding how the world itself works in 0.53. I am wondering what Happy and TSS events are exactly, but it will likely be explained in the future. Both are "canon" but i feel like Happy events are more likely to be "glitches", while TSS scenes are way more deliberate, which kinda leads to my next point.

So, Nao. It's heavily implied that she's Kaori's wish and if going by her very artistic drawing of a star being impregnated, she's aware of that fact too. And she seems to be somewhat attuned to the behind the scenes stuff, like "blackouts", TSS and whatnot. She went into one with Sensei and is somewhat often present when it happens to other characters.

My favourite incest gremlin. I actually like her latest character development, where she's clearly antagonistic and malicious, but not in a murderous (outside of reset) way (yet). So, she can't be factory reset because a god has a claim on her. Considering there's not a large pool of potential candidates i think it's either Nozomu or more likely Sekai who has at least two followers, i.e. Ami and Akira and going off the latest Akira/Nodoka/Sekai threesome, Nodoka is likely too. Tentatively Tsuneyo.

Also the game kinda implies a lot of things in a joking manner, namely Ami actually being Akira's daughter, but who knows. Also Sekai's body being actually buried under everblooming sakura tree in the Tsukioka manner, if we assume, that Sekai is indeed a god, the everblooming factor could be explained by that too.

Speaking of Tsukuiokas. Tsubasa was always kinda sus and if her minor Christmas slip up is any indication she is also aware of the resets and i won't put it past her to be aware from the start. Keeping all the abovementioned in mind, i also won't be surprised she knew Sekai when they all were younger and Sekai is "the third".

Wizards. Well, Sensei being Sensei, i also won't be surprised if we're getting either Chinami or Tsukasa or both, since they seem to kinda intertwined, sexually involved with Sensei soon'ish. But considering how easy it is to miss out on the whole thing entirely (and the first check is pretty early in the game) i am wondering what Sel's goal is.

And finally i am wondering what is the exact reason (or a combination of) for how Kumon-mi as a whole is recently turning into a very horny misery central.

Greetings, fellow thread-dwellers. It is I, everyone’s (least) favorite unmedicated schizo, back once again with a record-breaking super-duper long analysis (that was actually mostly written some time ago while I was on my “break” back in late December, but with the fast-approaching release date of 0.55, plus that whole thing that happened last time, I ultimately decided to postpone it until better days).

Now, most of what I’m about to say has already been individually mentioned at one point or another, usually as a casual observation or a small part of a larger post about something else, but I’ve never seen anyone compile and present it all as a single unified thesis through the lens of trying to analyze Selebus’ writing – which is exactly what I’m going to do here. So this colossal wall of text won’t contain any strange esoteric theories or “out there” concepts that require an ascended level of autism to understand – just a bunch of raw observations, partially filtered through my own perspective on the general story and its themes. Though it *will* contain an unhealthy amount of me glazing Selebus, so… trigger warning for that, I guess?

Also – and I deeply apologize for my behavior in advance, because I am fully aware that doing this on a public forum is somewhat of a bad tone – this analysis is, unfortunately, going to be posted as two separate parts: one main, one supplementary – because the second one ended up being just *that* fucking long. Both *are* relevant, I promise: this isn’t me just pointlessly extending the word count just for the sake of it, like some accuse Selebus of doing – but I *also* realize that you could technically maybe remove the “supplementary” part and still have a fairly complete understanding of everything I wanted to say, provided that you are perfectly willing to just kinda… take me at my word at one point and aren’t particularly interested in seeing the full detailed character studies, thematical comparisons and so on.

So people who only *mostly* care can just read the first part to get the main gist of it and completely ignore the second one, while those rare few media analysis enjoyers who *do* genuinely love thinking about the deeper intricacies of LiL’s writing – and also don’t mind reading actual thousands of words – will hopefully be able to appreciate the second part, as well.

To summarize this entire post in just a single sentence, Selebus is, effectively, a one (or, well, two) trick pony – though, despite how it might initially seem, I don’t mean this assessment of him an insult, but rather as something deserving of great praise.

While most writers have an entire arsenal of various useful cards up their sleeve: things they are especially proficient at, like worldbuilding, or romance, or what have you – this guy boldly pulls up to the table of high-rollers with only a single trump at his disposal, because he knows that this trump is a joker that he can easily turn into any card he wants. And so Selebus keeps using the same trick over, and over, and over again, building his entire game plan around this singular approach: specifically, his genuinely unparalleled mastery over the simple techniques of comparison and juxtaposition.

This mastery manifests in three distinct ways, which I am now going to go over one by one, providing relevant examples and other commentary where necessary:

The first (and the most obvious) one is the fact that every single character in Lessons in Love is intentionally introduced with a stereotype – a stereotype that is consistently *wrong*, without exception, and is then meticulously deconstructed with every new piece of information that you learn about that character. To put it in simpler terms, Selebus skillfully writes all of the introductions in such a way where meeting a new character (including Sensei) always follows the exact same process: you see them on screen for about five or so minutes, immediately get a fairly good first impression of “ah, okay, I understand what you are all about”, and then over the course of playing the game for 200+ hours slowly come to terms with the realization that your first impression was just flat-out wrong and that, no, you actually had *no fucking idea* what they were all about.

As with everything else, the twenty main girls are the clearest example of this – even doubly so, since ten of them got an additional “bonus stereotype for dummies” in the form of Maya’s journal. Just think back to how they were all introduced – the initial pictures that the game originally painted for them: Chika as a “basic” and vapid gyaru; Yumi as a callous and cruel bully; Ayane as a clingy and obsessive “I’m in love with Sensei, and it’s my only personality trait” girl; Sana as someone extremely shy, timid and reserved; Makoto as a smart and diligent class president who doesn’t care about anything except studying; Miku as a dumb hyperactive tomboy; Rin as an outgoing and happy-go-lucky gal with no personal problems besides being aggressively bisexual; Futaba as someone exceedingly nice and gentle, to the point of being unable to stand up for herself; Ami as an innocent and airheaded “girly girl”; Maya as cold and distant, and the sole bastion of “won’t be tempted to sleep with Sensei even in a million years”; Molly as a weeb-bait white gamer girl; Tsuneyo as a sheltered comic relief character; Uta as a flirt with a lot of self-confidence; Io as an asocial, asexual loner; Nodoka as a quirky incest-obsessed genius; Otoha as just… kind of normal; Touka as a walking-talking rich girl cliché; Yasu as a creepy religious nutcase; Noriko as a yandere-esque stalker with no filter; and Kirin as a hedonist who only cares about sex.

Now, how many of these “first impressions” are still on the mark? Or, better question yet: how many of them were *ever* on the mark, rather than just being a result of not having good enough understanding of that character as a person and/or a deliberate façade that they wear? I could keep going and continue onto the side cast, of course, but I think the point is more than clear: while most modern writers – “anime” writers especially – try to immediately make you understand (and thus get endeared/attached to) their characters through the liberal use of tropes and stereotypes, Selebus only *pretends* that he’s doing the same, before eventually forcing you to realize that, just like in real life, no one is ever that simple. That what you expect is *not* what you get – juxtaposition at its finest.

The second way in which Selebus masterfully utilizes his “comparison and juxtaposition” approach is directly related to the first one and, like it says in the title, can be best symbolized by a Venn diagram: pretty much every single long-established pair/trio of characters in LiL, whether they are relatives, friends, lovers, roommates, co-workers and so on (but *not* shit like Dorm Wars match-ups, which are mostly superficial and don’t have deeper implications), have been very deliberately coupled together due to their intentional similarities *and* differences in relation to a specific subject matter, so that these characters can both compliment and contrast with each other and thus further the narrative exploration of that particular unifying theme.

*Nothing* is accidental: if characters A and B (and, occasionally, C) share a relationship within the confines of the story, then they *will* form a Venn diagram of some kind, having some overlapping core idea that serves as a foundation for who they are that also manifests itself in drastically different ways. The greatest example of it is, obviously, Akira, who, like I already mentioned in one of my earliest posts, has a unique chemistry with literally every single female in the entire game, all of which showcase different sides of him and would take literally forever to analyze one-by-one… which is why I am *not* going to do that and will *instead* take literally forever going over all ten of the main Dorm pairings, plus a few additional ones at the very end.

(This is the “supplementary part” that I had to post as its own separate thing, so if you care about the exact specifics for why Selebus paired all of these characters together and how they all play off each other, you’ll find my detailed thoughts in “part 2” of this post. If you don’t, then no problem – feel free to ignore it entirely and just continue reading.)

Now, I fully anticipate that at least *some* of you have probably just rolled your eyes upon reading this title and had a strong exasperated reaction along the lines of “Jesus Christ… what the fuck is this asylum reject talking about now?”, but mathematical optimum – a term that I know because I am extremely pretentious (and also extensively studied applied mathematics) – is genuinely the most fitting concept to describe the third and final way comparison and juxtaposition are utilized by Selebus when it comes to LiL’s general narrative structure, and how he approaches writing the majority of important story beats.

For those unfamiliar, “mathematical optimum” refers to the “best” possible output value of a given mathematical function – an output that in many cases is only achievable on a singular set of corresponding input values. The process of finding that set (out of effectively infinite possible variations) and achieving said optimum is, subsequently, called optimization – which is *exactly* what Selebus is doing with LiL’s story, if you compare the game itself to a function, the story’s “quality” to that function’s output value, and various interactions between all of the game’s characters to the function’s input parameters.

Basically, Selebus’ entire creative process of coming up with new events consists of repeatedly asking himself the same single question: “What two (or, sometimes, three) complementary characters can I put together to produce the highest amount of narrative tension/character development possible at this current point in the story?” – and then doing exactly that. Once you notice this pattern, it becomes *really fucking hard* to un-notice it – it’s literally everywhere. Just in Chapter 4 alone we have:

> The fact that it was *specifically* Uta and Io who broke into Sensei’s apartment in “Rhythm of a Black Heart”, because if it was absolutely *any* other pair of girls who went there instead of these two (except for Maya and Noriko, who already knew about Akira’s wizard tendencies from their tutoring days), their responses to learning that extremely vital piece of information would have been entirely fucking different – and by “different” I mean “infinitely worse” – than the way both Dorm 7 roommates reacted to it: with twisted understanding and acceptance rather than shock and open disgust Akira would have gotten from pretty much anyone else.

> The 0.40 Camping Trip update, centered almost entirely around the concept of “family” and Akira finally finding enough resolve to become a proper father figure to Ami, followed *directly* by the 0.41 update, featuring three major Io events – Io, the uncontested winner of having the most negative outlook on parenthood in the entire game (for a very good reason), thus serving as the perfect antithesis to Akira “wow, being a parent sure is amazing” Arakawa – all of which ultimately resulted in what I personally consider to be the single best-written event in the entire game (thus far): the infamous “Stomachache”.

> Karin post-“Paranoid” initially dismissing all of Akira’s attempts to explain his blackouts as nothing more than pathetic excuses that only a truly naïve person would believe – until the 0.48 Touka/Yasu events, that is, where in “One of the Girls” Touka very unambiguously tells Karin that “oh, yeah, btw, our teacher has severe mental problems and occasionally loses control of himself – please be understanding of him whenever that happens”, greatly accelerating Karin’s forgiveness arc.

> Maki’s “Hello Alone” in 0.48, followed by “Thessalonians 4 (Lust Like the Pagans)” in 0.49, followed by Sara’s events in 0.50 – all in preparation for the grand “is it okay to sleep with teenagers?” debate of 0.54 that strongly divided the three close friends, thus leading into the rest of the Christmalloween events involving Haruka and Maki, as well as Maki’s current situation in 0.55.

> The entire 0.53 event chain (namely, the effect it had on Ayane) inadvertently serving as the catalyst for all three of Osako’s 0.55 events, especially “Pica” – which, through the underlying theme of motherhood, is then clearly linked with Wakana’s most recent event, “From the Horse’s Mouth”, where Ami (who is, arguably, still Ayane’s best friend) *also* brings up the idea of being a mom to Wakana, thus closing the thematical parallel between these four girls/women.

As well as many, many others – I could go on for at least a dozen more paragraphs, but doing so would be total overkill, so I’d rather stop there, hoping that these five examples were more than enough to prove my point. The whole game is structured like this: just an endless sequence of repeated character interactions, all deliberately selected to maximize the resulting dramatic/emotional effect. This line of logic also gives credence to my belief that Selebus doesn’t really “forget” things – he simply puts them on the backburner for the time being while developing *other* things, because good juxtaposition requires that *both* sides have been properly set-up, which is a fairly slow process when you’re just one guy with a limited time on your hands and an obligation to push out an update every month of the year single-handedly writing an insanely long story with a pretty large cast.

Aside from being primarily created for my own personal satisfaction first and foremost, this post also at least in part exists as a response to people who have been repeatedly criticizing many of Selebus’ decisions as a writer for the last couple of years (if not way longer than that) and expressing their severe dissatisfaction with the current state of LiL (aside from a few select “high points”, like the entirety of 0.53), arguing that the guy is just a pretentious hack who is only decent at best and is *definitely* nowhere near as good as he pretends to be.

Now, I am in no position to affect anyone’s subjective opinions regarding Lessons in Love’s story/characters, nor can I change their individual sensibilities when it comes to art as a whole: some people just fundamentally can’t stand long-winded philosophical monologues, for example, or have very little tolerance for abstract narratives that mostly focus on themes/symbolism rather than directly moving the plot forward – which is perfectly fine. And, obviously, attempting to gaslight anyone here (especially the regulars) that Selebus *isn’t* a huge narcissistic asshole would make me look like an utter fucking moron. What I *can* do, however, is to provide concrete and, hopefully, convincing examples of just how much thought and care he puts into writing his magnum opus, to try and dispel at least some of the doubts that LiL is somehow successful *in spite of* its creator and not *because of* him – you can like Selebus or you can hate him, sure, but give the guy credit where credit is due.

Just think back to how they were all introduced – the initial pictures that the game originally painted for them: Chika as a “basic” and vapid gyaru; Yumi as a callous and cruel bully; Ayane as a clingy and obsessive “I’m in love with Sensei, and it’s my only personality trait” girl; Sana as someone extremely shy, timid and reserved; Makoto as a smart and diligent class president who doesn’t care about anything except studying; Miku as a dumb hyperactive tomboy; Rin as an outgoing and happy-go-lucky gal with no personal problems besides being aggressively bisexual; Futaba as someone exceedingly nice and gentle, to the point of being unable to stand up for herself; Ami as an innocent and airheaded “girly girl”; Maya as cold and distant, and the sole bastion of “won’t be tempted to sleep with Sensei even in a million years”; Molly as a weeb-bait white gamer girl; Tsuneyo as a sheltered comic relief character; Uta as a flirt with a lot of self-confidence; Io as an asocial, asexual loner; Nodoka as a quirky incest-obsessed genius; Otoha as just… kind of normal; Touka as a walking-talking rich girl cliché; Yasu as a creepy religious nutcase; Noriko as a yandere-esque stalker with no filter; and Kirin as a hedonist who only cares about sex.
Now, how many of these “first impressions” are still on the mark? Or, better question yet: how many of them were *ever* on the mark, rather than just being a result of not having good enough understanding of that character as a person and/or a deliberate façade that they wear? I could keep going and continue onto the side cast, of course, but I think the point is more than clear: while most modern writers – “anime” writers especially – try to immediately make you understand (and thus get endeared/attached to) their characters through the liberal use of tropes and stereotypes, Selebus only *pretends* that he’s doing the same, before eventually forcing you to realize that, just like in real life, no one is ever that simple. The second way in which Selebus masterfully utilizes his “comparison and juxtaposition” approach is directly related to the first one and, like it says in the title, can be best symbolized by a Venn diagram: pretty much every single long-established pair/trio of characters in LiL, whether they are relatives, friends, lovers, roommates, co-workers and so on (but *not* shit like Dorm Wars match-ups, which are mostly superficial and don’t have deeper implications), have been very deliberately coupled together due to their intentional similarities *and* differences in relation to a specific subject matter, so that these characters can both compliment and contrast with each other and thus further the narrative exploration of that particular unifying theme.

Spoiler:
Mathematical Optimum
Now, I fully anticipate that at least *some* of you have probably just rolled your eyes upon reading this title and had a strong exasperated reaction along the lines of “Jesus Christ… what the fuck is this asylum reject talking about now?”, but mathematical optimum – a term that I know because I am extremely pretentious (and also extensively studied applied mathematics) – is genuinely the most fitting concept to describe the third and final way comparison and juxtaposition are utilized by Selebus when it comes to LiL’s general narrative structure, and how he approaches writing the majority of important story beats.
For those unfamiliar, “mathematical optimum” refers to the “best” possible output value of a given mathematical function – an output that in many cases is only achievable on a singular set of corresponding input values. The process of finding that set (out of effectively infinite possible variations) and achieving said optimum is, subsequently, called optimization – which is *exactly* what Selebus is doing with LiL’s story, if you compare the game itself to a function, the story’s “quality” to that function’s output value, and various interactions between all of the game’s characters to the function’s input parameters.
Basically, Selebus’ entire creative process of coming up with new events consists of repeatedly asking himself the same single question: “What two (or, sometimes, three) complementary characters can I put together to produce the highest amount of narrative tension/character development possible at this current point in the story?” – and then doing exactly that. Once you notice this pattern, it becomes *really fucking hard* to un-notice it – it’s literally everywhere. Just in Chapter 4 alone we have:
> The fact that it was *specifically* Uta and Io who broke into Sensei’s apartment in “Rhythm of a Black Heart”, because if it was absolutely *any* other pair of girls who went there instead of these two (except for Maya and Noriko, who already knew about Akira’s wizard tendencies from their tutoring days), their responses to learning that extremely vital piece of information would have been entirely fucking different – and by “different” I mean “infinitely worse” – than the way both Dorm 7 roommates reacted to it: with twisted understanding and acceptance rather than shock and open disgust Akira would have gotten from pretty much anyone else.
> The 0.40 Camping Trip update, centered almost entirely around the concept of “family” and Akira finally finding enough resolve to become a proper father figure to Ami, followed *directly* by the 0.41 update, featuring three major Io events – Io, the uncontested winner of having the most negative outlook on parenthood in the entire game (for a very good reason), thus serving as the perfect antithesis to Akira “wow, being a parent sure is amazing” Arakawa – all of which ultimately resulted in what I personally consider to be the single best-written event in the entire game (thus far): the infamous “Stomachache”.
> Karin post-“Paranoid” initially dismissing all of Akira’s attempts to explain his blackouts as nothing more than pathetic excuses that only a truly naïve person would believe – until the 0.48 Touka/Yasu events, that is, where in “One of the Girls” Touka very unambiguously tells Karin that “oh, yeah, btw, our teacher has severe mental problems and occasionally loses control of himself – please be understanding of him whenever that happens”, greatly accelerating Karin’s forgiveness arc.
> Maki’s “Hello Alone” in 0.48, followed by “Thessalonians 4 (Lust Like the Pagans)” in 0.49, followed by Sara’s events in 0.50 – all in preparation for the grand “is it okay to sleep with teenagers?” debate of 0.54 that strongly divided the three close friends, thus leading into the rest of the Christmalloween events involving Haruka and Maki, as well as Maki’s current situation in 0.55.
> The entire 0.53 event chain (namely, the effect it had on Ayane) inadvertently serving as the catalyst for all three of Osako’s 0.55 events, especially “Pica” – which, through the underlying theme of motherhood, is then clearly linked with Wakana’s most recent event, “From the Horse’s Mouth”, where Ami (who is, arguably, still Ayane’s best friend) *also* brings up the idea of being a mom to Wakana, thus closing the thematical parallel between these four girls/women.
As well as many, many others – I could go on for at least a dozen more paragraphs, but doing so would be total overkill, so I’d rather stop there, hoping that these five examples were more than enough to prove my point. The whole game is structured like this: just an endless sequence of repeated character interactions, all deliberately selected to maximize the resulting dramatic/emotional effect. This line of logic also gives credence to my belief that Selebus doesn’t really “forget” things – he simply puts them on the backburner for the time being while developing *other* things, because good juxtaposition requires that *both* sides have been properly set-up, which is a fairly slow process when you’re just one guy with a limited time on your hands and an obligation to push out an update every month of the year single-handedly writing an insanely long story with a pretty large cast.
Spoiler:
Finishing thoughts
Aside from being primarily created for my own personal satisfaction first and foremost, this post also at least in part exists as a response to people who have been repeatedly criticizing many of Selebus’ decisions as a writer for the last couple of years (if not way longer than that) and expressing their severe dissatisfaction with the current state of LiL (aside from a few select “high points”, like the entirety of 0.53), arguing that the guy is just a pretentious hack who is only decent at best and is *definitely* nowhere near as good as he pretends to be.
Now, I am in no position to affect anyone’s subjective opinions regarding Lessons in Love’s story/characters, nor can I change their individual sensibilities when it comes to art as a whole: some people just fundamentally can’t stand long-winded philosophical monologues, for example, or have very little tolerance for abstract narratives that mostly focus on themes/symbolism rather than directly moving the plot forward – which is perfectly fine. And, obviously, attempting to gaslight anyone here (especially the regulars) that Selebus *isn’t* a huge narcissistic asshole would make me look like an utter fucking moron. What I *can* do, however, is to provide concrete and, hopefully, convincing examples of just how much thought and care he puts into writing his magnum opus, to try and dispel at least some of the doubts that LiL is somehow successful *in spite of* its creator and not *because of* him – you can like Selebus or you can hate him, sure, but give the guy credit where credit is due.

> Maki’s “Hello Alone” in 0.48, followed by “Thessalonians 4 (Lust Like the Pagans)” in 0.49, followed by Sara’s events in 0.50 – all in preparation for the grand “is it okay to sleep with teenagers?” debate of 0.54 that strongly divided the three close friends, thus leading into the rest of the Christmalloween events involving Haruka and Maki, as well as Maki’s current situation in 0.55.
> The entire 0.53 event chain (namely, the effect it had on Ayane) inadvertently serving as the catalyst for all three of Osako’s 0.55 events, especially “Pica” – which, through the underlying theme of motherhood, is then clearly linked with Wakana’s most recent event, “From the Horse’s Mouth”, where Ami (who is, arguably, still Ayane’s best friend) *also* brings up the idea of being a mom to Wakana, thus closing the thematical parallel between these four girls/women.
As well as many, many others – I could go on for at least a dozen more paragraphs, but doing so would be total overkill, so I’d rather stop there, hoping that these five examples were more than enough to prove my point. The whole game is structured like this: just an endless sequence of repeated character interactions, all deliberately selected to maximize the resulting dramatic/emotional effect. This line of logic also gives credence to my belief that Selebus doesn’t really “forget” things – he simply puts them on the backburner for the time being while developing *other* things, because good juxtaposition requires that *both* sides have been properly set-up, which is a fairly slow process when you’re just one guy with a limited time on your hands and an obligation to push out an update every month of the year single-handedly writing an insanely long story with a pretty large cast.

spoilers.title: Finishing thoughts
spoilers.html:
Aside from being primarily created for my own personal satisfaction first and foremost, this post also at least in part exists as a response to people who have been repeatedly criticizing many of Selebus’ decisions as a writer for the last couple of years (if not way longer than that) and expressing their severe dissatisfaction with the current state of LiL (aside from a few select “high points”, like the entirety of 0.53), arguing that the guy is just a pretentious hack who is only decent at best and is *definitely* nowhere near as good as he pretends to be.

Now, I am in no position to affect anyone’s subjective opinions regarding Lessons in Love’s story/characters, nor can I change their individual sensibilities when it comes to art as a whole: some people just fundamentally can’t stand long-winded philosophical monologues, for example, or have very little tolerance for abstract narratives that mostly focus on themes/symbolism rather than directly moving the plot forward – which is perfectly fine. And, obviously, attempting to gaslight anyone here (especially the regulars) that Selebus *isn’t* a huge narcissistic asshole would make me look like an utter fucking moron. What I *can* do, however, is to provide concrete and, hopefully, convincing examples of just how much thought and care he puts into writing his magnum opus, to try and dispel at least some of the doubts that LiL is somehow successful *in spite of* its creator and not *because of* him – you can like Selebus or you can hate him, sure, but give the guy credit where credit is due.
