Hello friends. I've had a busy month and missed out on the initial 0.55 discussion, but there's something I'd still like to talk about: the newest hints about Rin's biological family. Onund asked her about her bio mom, revealing some things in the process:
View attachment 5663983 View attachment 5663984 View attachment 5663985
I could be wrong, but I think he's also talking about Rin's secret sister in this passage. I'm going to start the discussion there.
The Rokuharas have said that Rin's dad was a "huge cheat" and may have had another family. It's fairly likely that he had other children and that someone found out about it - otherwise how would the Rokuharas know?

With that in mind, it makes a lot of sense to me that Onund's phrase "another you" refers to a half-sister of Rin. Finding out that such a person exists would be a big deal to Rin's mom, because it would also mean finding out that her "partner" isn't just unfaithful, he's been hiding a whole second family. That kind of shock could cause her to "leave" (more on this in the next section).

For those that don't know, I (and many others) believe that Rin and Sana are half-sisters. Sana is also a perfect fit for the other clues that Onund gives:
  • She's smaller than Rin.
  • She's more broken than Rin. (Understatement of the year)
  • There's something special about her that the gods want.
  • Gods who are more important than Onund have been trying to secure her favor.
Pegasus has made multiple attempts to get her to give herself to him, similar to what Onund does with Rin in her TSS. Pegasus is supposedly a Peerless One, making him important in the hierarchy of gods (although I have doubts about his legitimacy).

View attachment 5663992 View attachment 5663994 View attachment 5663995 View attachment 5663996

It's not just Pegasus; Sana said other gods have been doing the same thing, and Sekaori/USER3 seem very interested in getting her to accept any god at all.

View attachment 5663997 View attachment 5663998
View attachment 5664004 View attachment 5664005

Sana has something they want, something that's probably intrinsic to her since her mother went through the same thing when she was younger.

View attachment 5664006 View attachment 5664007
The only other character I can think of to fit these clues is Ami, but we haven't seen direct evidence of gods trying to gain her favor like with Sana. Add that to all of the preexisting hints of Sana's connection to Rin, and it's far more likely to be her.
The claim that Rin's bio mom "left" is interesting, because from what we know she never physically went anywhere, certainly not by choice. She was forced to give Rin up for adoption because her mental issues made her unable to raise a child on her own, and it's implied (or possibly outright stated, I don't remember) that she was institutionalized somewhere.

There's another possible meaning, though: she left mentally, in much the same way that Sensei's mind can slip to other worlds during his blackouts. While Sensei always returns from his mental slips, we know that it's possible for a slip to be one-way, for someone's mind to get stuck somewhere else - something like that happened to Kyoko Nagasawa. And there's a similarity in how Rin's mom "could barely speak" and how Kyoko is unable to respond to Nodoka.

Sensei's blackouts are often triggered by mental distress, when some aspect of his trauma gets dredged up. I'm guessing the shock of finding out that Rin's dad had a second family served as a similar trigger for Rin's mom, causing her mind to retreat from the situation.


A couple questions occur to me based on the above hints. These are very speculative and probably don't go anywhere, but they're worth thinking about.

1. If Rin's mom found out about Sara's family, did Sara find out about Rin's mom?
A long time ago Sara said that someone eventually found out about her relationship with her teacher, but we've never learned who that was or what the consequences were. Maybe it was Rin's mom. Sara did also say that she never knew who any of her teacher's other girls were, which would seem to preclude that, but after her most recent events I wouldn't put it past her to lie about inconvenient truths. For example, if she feels some guilt for Rin's mom going insane, I could see her pretending it never happened.

2. If Rin's mom (mentally) went somewhere else, have we seen any clues about who she is or where she ended up?
Onund asks Rin what her mother is doing right now, hinting that her present circumstances could be relevant to the story. Given the similarities with Kyoko Nagasawa, could she be one of the other girls in the upside down house? The LiL laws of genetics probably point against that - the other UDH girls have very different hair and/or eye colors from Rin. Here's the real tinfoil thought: what if her mother is Kyoko Nagasawa? Again, probably not, as I can't remember the narrators ever hinting that Kyoko could have a second daughter.

Are there any other possibilities that I'm forgetting, or are we to assume that Rin's mom exited the story completely when she "left", and wherever she is now isn't relevant?
I don't think Onund's comments tell us anything new about Rin's dad, but there was foreshadowing about him in a different event.

View attachment 5664027 View attachment 5664029 View attachment 5664030

This is the exact same type of foreshadowing that I talked about in this post. In particular:

1. Yet again someone says that Sensei is old enough to be Rin's dad (ish). This idea has been expressed multiple times for Sana and for Rin, but not at all for any other character.

2. Rika asks what would happen if Rin were to learn that she's related to Sensei ("not much" is apparently the answer). This is very similar to stuff that has been hinted at for Sana, and I think in each case it foreshadows a future reveal that they actually are related.

These reinforce my belief that Sana and Rin have the same father, and he's somehow closely connected to Sensei. For my money, Nozomu Arakawa is still the most likely possibility.

Plus, Rin's admission that she'd still fuck Sensei even if he was her biological dad is just more evidence she's an Arakawa. That family fucking loves incest.
I also noticed something in Rin's TSS which I don't think anyone has brought up yet: while she was with Onund, they were being watched by The Orb.
View attachment 5664039 View attachment 5664041
(It also looks like there is a second round, black thing above and behind Rin's head, but it's not clear what.)

For now, my best guess is this is just symbolic. The Orb in Sensei Quest was a manifestation of the "dark entity" that Sensei mentally struggles with, and Rin has her own dark entity. So in Rin's TSS we have a reminder of her dark entity, represented by The Orb for thematic reasons.
When Sensei fought The Orb he was told that it was the "dark entity" inside of him. (I argued here that it's a manifestation of his despair after Sekai died in the original timeline).

View attachment 5664044 View attachment 5664045

The idea of a "dark entity" has also been linked to Rin, and in particular her depression.

View attachment 5664050 View attachment 5664051 View attachment 5664057 View attachment 5664058

Though more recently it might be feeding her obsession with Sensei.

View attachment 5664059 View attachment 5664060 View attachment 5664070 View attachment 5664071
An interesting thought: is her sexual obsession a new method for escaping the feelings (or lack thereof) that she used to deal with by cutting herself? I do think it's been an unusually long time since her last episode (I vaguely recall this being said in-game, but I could be imagining it). Using sex as a coping mechanism is also a classic Arakawa trait.
There could be a literal meaning to The Orb's presence, though. In addition to being Sensei's dark entity, The Orb was also "GOD", the combined trinity. It's presence here could show the users messing with Rin's mental state. Maybe they're making her unnaturally horny like they did to Sana in Chapter 3?


Including the orb, there are quite a few references to holes in Rin's TSS:
  • The Orb looks like a void of pure emptiness and in particular is the hole left by the missing "moon".
  • In it's first appearance, The Orb was accompanied by constant use of the audio file theholelol.mp3
  • The event's renders are labelled rinmeetsthehole.
  • Onund is the God of the Hole.
  • Rin ends up in the Room with Clocks after reaching into Onund's hole.
  • Rin meets Onund after being thrown into the Heavenly Pit, which the wiki claims is the sinkhole of that name that really exists in China.
On top of that, this is the same update that includes Io's expedition to explore the hole in the tunnels, which we learned is different from the sinkhole that swallowed the other school. I don't know if any of this means anything, but Selebus sure seems to have had fun with it.


The wiki claims Onund is from China and there's some Chinese text/speech in the TSS. I don't think anyone shared a translation yet, so here you go (These are also spoken as onund[1-3].mp3):
View attachment 5664086
走 近 一 点 : "Come a little closer"
View attachment 5664088
我 已经 长大 了 : "I have grown up" (this is according to google - I assume a more generic "I have grown" is intended)
View attachment 5664092
全世界 都 会 知道 真相 : "The whole world will know the truth"
Finally, I want to say that I view HOPE's recent appearances differently than other people seem to. I would be very surprised if HPGL (HOPE, Peerless God of Light) is actually the same entity as the HOPE who showed up in the first two chapters. It's unlikely HPGL existed in that name/form before the seventh reset. And neither of the HOPEs is the genuine (original) USER1, though they both were/are trying to become a new one.

I've wanted to write about USER1 for quite a while, but it's a big undertaking since there are lots of little parts that only start to make sense when you look at the full picture. I'll probably need to do another playthrough first and I'm not sure when I'll find time for that.

spoilers.title: Rin's sister
spoilers.html:
The Rokuharas have said that Rin's dad was a "huge cheat" and may have had another family. It's fairly likely that he had other children and that someone found out about it - otherwise how would the Rokuharas know?

With that in mind, it makes a lot of sense to me that Onund's phrase "another you" refers to a half-sister of Rin. Finding out that such a person exists would be a big deal to Rin's mom, because it would also mean finding out that her "partner" isn't just unfaithful, he's been hiding a whole second family. That kind of shock could cause her to "leave" (more on this in the next section).

For those that don't know, I (and many others) believe that Rin and Sana are half-sisters. Sana is also a perfect fit for the other clues that Onund gives:
  • She's smaller than Rin.
  • She's more broken than Rin. (Understatement of the year)
  • There's something special about her that the gods want.
  • Gods who are more important than Onund have been trying to secure her favor.
Pegasus has made multiple attempts to get her to give herself to him, similar to what Onund does with Rin in her TSS. Pegasus is supposedly a Peerless One, making him important in the hierarchy of gods (although I have doubts about his legitimacy).

View attachment 5663992 View attachment 5663994 View attachment 5663995 View attachment 5663996

It's not just Pegasus; Sana said other gods have been doing the same thing, and Sekaori/USER3 seem very interested in getting her to accept any god at all.

View attachment 5663997 View attachment 5663998
View attachment 5664004 View attachment 5664005

Sana has something they want, something that's probably intrinsic to her since her mother went through the same thing when she was younger.

View attachment 5664006 View attachment 5664007
The only other character I can think of to fit these clues is Ami, but we haven't seen direct evidence of gods trying to gain her favor like with Sana. Add that to all of the preexisting hints of Sana's connection to Rin, and it's far more likely to be her.

spoilers.title: Rin's mom
spoilers.html:
The claim that Rin's bio mom "left" is interesting, because from what we know she never physically went anywhere, certainly not by choice. She was forced to give Rin up for adoption because her mental issues made her unable to raise a child on her own, and it's implied (or possibly outright stated, I don't remember) that she was institutionalized somewhere.

There's another possible meaning, though: she left mentally, in much the same way that Sensei's mind can slip to other worlds during his blackouts. While Sensei always returns from his mental slips, we know that it's possible for a slip to be one-way, for someone's mind to get stuck somewhere else - something like that happened to Kyoko Nagasawa. And there's a similarity in how Rin's mom "could barely speak" and how Kyoko is unable to respond to Nodoka.

Sensei's blackouts are often triggered by mental distress, when some aspect of his trauma gets dredged up. I'm guessing the shock of finding out that Rin's dad had a second family served as a similar trigger for Rin's mom, causing her mind to retreat from the situation.

aramaug said:
Hello friends. I've had a busy month and missed out on the initial 0.55 discussion, but there's something I'd still like to talk about: the newest hints about Rin's biological family. Onund asked her about her bio mom, revealing some things in the process:
Click to expand...
Amazing stuff! To be honest, I don’t really have much to add to the theory itself (it was clearly high-effort in addition to being both extremely well-presented and well-argued, thus making all of your conclusions feel fairly convincing), though it *did* made me think of a few tangentially relevant things, mostly about The Orb:

Now, I’m almost 100% certain that at least one person *must have* already brought this up before at some point and I’m simply blacking out on it happening, so sorry if what I’m about to say is going to be completely old news to everyone, but it kinda just hit me: if we take the Ancient Orb/GOD in “Restart” to be the “true/combined” form of all four Gods (including the fourth yet unnamed one that seemingly awakens in “All For You”), then it stands to reason that each of the Four Elemental Orbs that Akira collects during “SENSEI-QUEST” must *also* be referencing each individual member of… the Tetrarchy (I guess?):

– The Orb of Plant is pretty clearly related to Tenchou: there is the obvious “stairs” connection (the location where you obtain it is called “Sea of Stairs”, and Tenchou is the God who is associated with stairs the most, as I already pointed out in one of my recent posts), the fact that almost all of the Plant Council meetings that we’ve seen all took place in front of that strange ramen restaurant near the beach (once again, connecting them to Tenchou), and, finally, the curious detail that the guardian of that particular Orb – Net With Knife Nose & Melon Mouth – first appears during the event that prominently involves USER2 (“Backwards Dancing”) and is then subsequently defeated in battle using “The Sword of Hope” – a sword that just so happens to bear the name of Tenchou’s prime nemesis.

– The Orb of Worm is equally clearly related to HOPE, just based on the “worm” association alone. Plus, you know, it makes a lot of sense for the guardian of HOPE’s Orb to be a maggot, since they thrive in the heat and mainly breed during summer – HOPE’s season.

– Now, the Orb of Fist is, admittedly, hard to meaningfully connect to any of the Gods, since none of them exactly have “fists” (or “karate”, or “combat”, or anything of the sort) as a part of their known symbology, but the Random Karate Person *does* at one point mention “the bell that summons the great frog” – clearly referencing the giant frog that apparently sleeps at the center of the Great Pareidolia Mall – so, with no better alternatives, I’ll say that this Orb is related to Pareidolia and just leave it at that.

– Which leaves us with the Orb of Red, guarded by the Red Twins in the Unholy Cathedral – meaning that, through a process of elimination, this Orb is supposed to embody the final, fourth God: the one who “sings in its sleep”, the unnamed shadow “that emerges from the hole in a wall”. Curiously, Youdidit and Moyo are the only Orb guardians that Sensei doesn’t actually defeat: instead, they willingly sacrifice themselves to the “Dark Entity”, because that is apparently something that “must be done to progress Sensei-Quest”. Does this mean anything? Probably – and I have my own personal theories on what the importance of that distinction could be, in addition to the question of the twins’ true allegiance, beyond them just being freelancers currently employed by HOPE – but I don’t intend to mention any of them here, since it would all just be unsubstantiated guessing at the end of the day.

And with that, we fully leave the field of actual relevancy and say bye-bye to logical observations based on factual evidence, because the next part of my post stretches the meaning of the word “tangential” to its utmost limits:

Once upon a time, in the comment section of that one five-hour-long LiL “analysis” video made by some Russian guy that was very briefly discussed in this thread about a year ago, I intentionally compared Lessons in Love to one of my favorite books: “Demian: The Story of Emil Sinclair’s Youth” by Hermann Hesse. That particular comparison was mostly in relation to the common duality of “Realm of Light” vs “Realm of Darkness” these two stories share and the analogous way they explore the subject of conventional morality, but since that entire discussion unfortunately took place while I was still very early into my second re-read of LiL (and, thus, still had only an extremely basic understanding of the meta-level references and allusions contained within the text), I completely missed yet *another* equally strong similarity to “Demian”: the repeated symbolic motif of eggs, birds and “destroying the world”. After all, the most famous quote from that book is:

“The bird fights its way out of the egg. The egg is the world. Who would be born, must first destroy a world. The bird flies to God – that God’s name is Abraxas.”

Now, to preface: do I *actually* think that Selebus took direct inspiration from Hesse’s work? No, not really – although there *is* the Hindu “Maya” connection, plus a lot of other similar Gnostic/Jungian theming, so who really knows at this point. Nonetheless, what is *truly* important here is that the line

“If God or god exists, I think It or it needs to be everything: I don’t think we’re allowed to choose one or the other – in fact, I think the others as a whole are not so whole at all”

that is uttered by (I believe) Sekai in “All For You” during the scene related to the fourth entity is *the perfect* description of Abraxas: the God who is the world itself, who reveals itself to you in your deepest, most primordial dreams; the God who embodies both good and evil, virtue and sin, light and darkness, creation and destruction – all in equal measure.

To worship Abraxas is to independently walk the path of self-reflection and self-actualization with your head held high, no matter where it leads: whether to a long and prosperous life or an early grave; whether you’ll be labeled a saint or a sinner. It means accepting the existence of opposing forces both within yourself and in the world at large and realizing that *both* are necessary: that blindly praising the “good” things and blindly condemning the “bad” things means inherently ignoring the true picture of reality, and that intentionally starving the beast inside your heart for the sake of “being a good person” is just as bad as freely indulging it without reserve.

If any of this sounds even remotely familiar to you, that means that you’ve probably read at least *some* of my previous esoteric ramblings (and if so, thank you!), since that’s the exact same ideological prism that I have been using to analyze LiL all this time (seen most clearly in my “LiL is a group therapy session with Nodoka as a therapist” schizo post). Because, yeah, most of it surprisingly fits together in a pretty neat way when you try to find some direct thematic parallels between these two seemingly disconnected narratives:

– Akira is the Sinclair of this story: the protagonist who possesses the Mark of Cain (the ability to bend both the circumstances and the people around him to his will) and most strongly embodies the conflict of “Realm of Light” vs “Realm of Darkness”, constantly jumping between extreme abstinence and extreme indulgence, all the while waffling in self-pity and indecision; he is the “bird” who needs to “break the egg” (actually seen at the very end of “The Room With Clocks”, which results in Sensei “becoming whole once more”) by walking the full path of self-actualization, thus “destroying the world” (the artificial reality of Kumon-mi) and “flying towards Abraxas” (his real life outside of the Resets where he is “complete”, regardless of what form that “completeness” takes).

– Nodoka is Akira’s Demian: Sinclair’s part-equal, part-guide who *already* walks the path of Abraxas and consciously, with no hesitation or doubt, exercises the power of the Mark of Cain in order to achieve the results they want, all for the sake of understanding the deeper truth of this world (which they achieve through incessant research and constant self-reflection, as well as through meaningful, borderline prophetic dreams). Likewise, both Nodoka and Demian are strongly defined by their relationships with their mothers: Kyoko and Frau Eva are in equal parts “prototypes” and role models for their respective children, as well as some of the only beacons of genuine human connection for them, considering that Nodoka/Demian are otherwise extremely individualistic and independent people who are fairly callous and rarely truly open their hearts to others.

– Kumon-mi, alongside the Resets, is quite literally “maya’s world” (“maya” in the Hindu sense: “an illusion where things appear to be present but are not what they seem” and “that which is constantly changing and thus is spiritually unreal”) – a clear analogue to Sinclair’s “Scheinwelt”: the "world of illusion” that he lives in most of his early years, placed in direct opposition to the “world of spiritual truth” that he eventually discovers and dedicates his life to pursuing.

– Maya herself (Prime, that is) decently fits in the role of Pistorius: an older, wiser mentor figure with direct connections to both religion and music (Pistorius was a theology student dropout and an organist who played during off hours at a local church, Maya is a miko who reluctantly serves at her local shrine and used to play violin in the past) who teaches the protagonist the basics truths of the world and shows him the path that he must walk, yet they themselves are too bound by their circumstances and too set in their ways to actually follow their own advice and reach enlightenment on their own.

– And, finally, the Trinity are the false, “makeshift” Gods, imperfect and incomplete. Each of them embodies only a *part* of our world, rather than the entirety of it; they create division, split that which should be whole into conflicting parts: light and darkness, heat and cold, summer and winter, callousness and concern. Thus, the fate of these broken fragments is to be eventually reunited once more and become the singular entity that contains everything and nothing at all: the capital ‘G’ GOD.

spoilers.title: The Egg, The Bird and The World (the real schizo hours)
spoilers.html:
Once upon a time, in the comment section of that one five-hour-long LiL “analysis” video made by some Russian guy that was very briefly discussed in this thread about a year ago, I intentionally compared Lessons in Love to one of my favorite books: “Demian: The Story of Emil Sinclair’s Youth” by Hermann Hesse. That particular comparison was mostly in relation to the common duality of “Realm of Light” vs “Realm of Darkness” these two stories share and the analogous way they explore the subject of conventional morality, but since that entire discussion unfortunately took place while I was still very early into my second re-read of LiL (and, thus, still had only an extremely basic understanding of the meta-level references and allusions contained within the text), I completely missed yet *another* equally strong similarity to “Demian”: the repeated symbolic motif of eggs, birds and “destroying the world”. After all, the most famous quote from that book is:

“The bird fights its way out of the egg. The egg is the world. Who would be born, must first destroy a world. The bird flies to God – that God’s name is Abraxas.”

Now, to preface: do I *actually* think that Selebus took direct inspiration from Hesse’s work? No, not really – although there *is* the Hindu “Maya” connection, plus a lot of other similar Gnostic/Jungian theming, so who really knows at this point. Nonetheless, what is *truly* important here is that the line

“If God or god exists, I think It or it needs to be everything: I don’t think we’re allowed to choose one or the other – in fact, I think the others as a whole are not so whole at all”

that is uttered by (I believe) Sekai in “All For You” during the scene related to the fourth entity is *the perfect* description of Abraxas: the God who is the world itself, who reveals itself to you in your deepest, most primordial dreams; the God who embodies both good and evil, virtue and sin, light and darkness, creation and destruction – all in equal measure.

To worship Abraxas is to independently walk the path of self-reflection and self-actualization with your head held high, no matter where it leads: whether to a long and prosperous life or an early grave; whether you’ll be labeled a saint or a sinner. It means accepting the existence of opposing forces both within yourself and in the world at large and realizing that *both* are necessary: that blindly praising the “good” things and blindly condemning the “bad” things means inherently ignoring the true picture of reality, and that intentionally starving the beast inside your heart for the sake of “being a good person” is just as bad as freely indulging it without reserve.

If any of this sounds even remotely familiar to you, that means that you’ve probably read at least *some* of my previous esoteric ramblings (and if so, thank you!), since that’s the exact same ideological prism that I have been using to analyze LiL all this time (seen most clearly in my “LiL is a group therapy session with Nodoka as a therapist” schizo post). Because, yeah, most of it surprisingly fits together in a pretty neat way when you try to find some direct thematic parallels between these two seemingly disconnected narratives:

– Akira is the Sinclair of this story: the protagonist who possesses the Mark of Cain (the ability to bend both the circumstances and the people around him to his will) and most strongly embodies the conflict of “Realm of Light” vs “Realm of Darkness”, constantly jumping between extreme abstinence and extreme indulgence, all the while waffling in self-pity and indecision; he is the “bird” who needs to “break the egg” (actually seen at the very end of “The Room With Clocks”, which results in Sensei “becoming whole once more”) by walking the full path of self-actualization, thus “destroying the world” (the artificial reality of Kumon-mi) and “flying towards Abraxas” (his real life outside of the Resets where he is “complete”, regardless of what form that “completeness” takes).

– Nodoka is Akira’s Demian: Sinclair’s part-equal, part-guide who *already* walks the path of Abraxas and consciously, with no hesitation or doubt, exercises the power of the Mark of Cain in order to achieve the results they want, all for the sake of understanding the deeper truth of this world (which they achieve through incessant research and constant self-reflection, as well as through meaningful, borderline prophetic dreams). Likewise, both Nodoka and Demian are strongly defined by their relationships with their mothers: Kyoko and Frau Eva are in equal parts “prototypes” and role models for their respective children, as well as some of the only beacons of genuine human connection for them, considering that Nodoka/Demian are otherwise extremely individualistic and independent people who are fairly callous and rarely truly open their hearts to others.

– Kumon-mi, alongside the Resets, is quite literally “maya’s world” (“maya” in the Hindu sense: “an illusion where things appear to be present but are not what they seem” and “that which is constantly changing and thus is spiritually unreal”) – a clear analogue to Sinclair’s “Scheinwelt”: the "world of illusion” that he lives in most of his early years, placed in direct opposition to the “world of spiritual truth” that he eventually discovers and dedicates his life to pursuing.

– Maya herself (Prime, that is) decently fits in the role of Pistorius: an older, wiser mentor figure with direct connections to both religion and music (Pistorius was a theology student dropout and an organist who played during off hours at a local church, Maya is a miko who reluctantly serves at her local shrine and used to play violin in the past) who teaches the protagonist the basics truths of the world and shows him the path that he must walk, yet they themselves are too bound by their circumstances and too set in their ways to actually follow their own advice and reach enlightenment on their own.

– And, finally, the Trinity are the false, “makeshift” Gods, imperfect and incomplete. Each of them embodies only a *part* of our world, rather than the entirety of it; they create division, split that which should be whole into conflicting parts: light and darkness, heat and cold, summer and winter, callousness and concern. Thus, the fate of these broken fragments is to be eventually reunited once more and become the singular entity that contains everything and nothing at all: the capital ‘G’ GOD.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just a few days ago, after I happened to read Sel’s analysis of the “stray cat” section in the care packages, I developed some deep doubts about Himawari’s setting.

First of all, here Sel is clearly saying that this is the original scarf she once had, not just some random replacement. And to me, this immediately creates a huge problem: it means that Himawari can travel to any point in time. In my view, this is absolutely disastrous for the story’s internal logic. I mean, Himawari can now exist simultaneously in the past, the present, and the future. That’s basically omniscience and omnipotence. Then what’s even the point of watching the livestream? With such overwhelming power, the only things she ends up doing are… delivering a scarf to accelerate Maya’s death? Sending a watermelon when amifinger == true?
But in Untitled, she seems completely powerless again, as if she has no idea what’s going to happen in the future. If you really know the future, shouldn’t you already know that Akira will successfully escape?Especially in 0.53, she’s portrayed as equally helpless, as if she’s just trying things blindly, which is the total opposite of her usual all-knowing image.Logically speaking, she should at least be aware of all the events that happened before 0.53,right ?This is such a contradiction in the setting, and such a lack of rigor. Honestly, I suspect Sel never thought this through at all, and just thought the whole “scarf closed loop” was cool.
I honestly still don’t know what Sel’s definition of himawari.co even is. First of all, Himawari is an employee of a giant corporation (Shiawase Group?), but “.co” very obviously implies a company. Does this mean that himawari.co is a company created in the far future by the future version of Himawari? That would imply a future where the project of interdimensional travel agency is successfully realized. And since this company shows up so often in the story, does that mean that the future of the future Himawari is also interfering with the present? Or is it simply that Sel thinks himawari.co is just a codename for Himawari, nothing more?

You've fallen into the trap of thinking, from a story POV, that just because you're outside of an event, you can know it's start, it's finish, AND all the steps in between.

Akira's story is a puzzle with a million pieces. It has a defined start, but with a near infinite variation, how you get to the defined ending is impossible to full predict, even for someone that know how it's supposed to end.

Imagine, if you will, that you have a deck of cards in your hands. You deal yourself a hand of 5 cards, and it comes up, miraculously, as a Royal Flush. It's the perfect hand! A Straight, A Flush, and all face cards.

Now imagine that some mysterious God has decided that you're locked in a time maze until you can deal that hand to yourself again, blindfolded, when someone else is shuffling the deck. You can't die, you can't escape, until you manage to pull that Royal Flush all over again...

Lucky for you, you have a time traveling daughter that can help, but never too directly, for fear that the mad god will destroy everything. She knows that eventually you escape the maze, since she exists, so somehow, someway, you eventually land on the perfect shuffle that lets you re-deal that perfect hand...but she has no idea when. So...she does what she can to subtly influence the shuffle. A nudge here, a push there, hoping that the right sequence will end things so she can stop watching you and everyone she loves suffer. Every change she makes, she can look forward and see how it ends up, but only by direct observation...but she can't see every step in between, not without experiencing it directly. It's not a direct information upload, she has to actively watch it happen.

It's omniscience and omnipotence, you're right...but it's the worst kind of torture. Knowing how a story ends, but not knowing how it got from Point A to Point Z, and every time it gets to Point T it starts all over again at Point A?

Storywise, it still works. Time Travel stories almost always fall into the fallacy of 'changing' the past to effect the present, and the future...but if you exist in the future, to observe the past, than the present has ALWAYS existed in the form you see it. The events you try to change were already changed simply by you existing. What you saw, is how the world is, no matter what changes you make in the past.

I wrote an allegory recently in a Harry Potter discussion that I think fits well here:

Imagine you had a Time Turner. You wake up, and decide to go visit a friend. You spend all day there, and come home. Once home, you remember that you're out of your life saving medicine, and were supposed to pick some up at the store. Store is closed...so you use your Time Turner to go back in time to 4pm, when the store was open, to get your medicine.

At this exact moment, TWO of you exist. Version A, Version B.

Version A is at the friends house. They are past you.
Version B is at the store, picking up the medicine. This is present you.

Version A becomes Version B. Version B has always existed, even when Version A was at the friends house. Version B can never interact with Version A, because Version B would REMEMBER that, WHEN they were Version A. Since they don't, it never happened. Version B will always make it home after Version A has gone back in time, otherwise they would remember seeing Version B, when they were Version A, and experiencing the Present.

This gets much more complicated when you allow for outside observation and changes, but that only affects the person that is outside. The person inside will always be experiencing time and events as they happened within the bubble. Every loop is a closed loop simply by existing.

spoilers.title: Time Travel Rant
spoilers.html:
You've fallen into the trap of thinking, from a story POV, that just because you're outside of an event, you can know it's start, it's finish, AND all the steps in between.

Akira's story is a puzzle with a million pieces. It has a defined start, but with a near infinite variation, how you get to the defined ending is impossible to full predict, even for someone that know how it's supposed to end.

Imagine, if you will, that you have a deck of cards in your hands. You deal yourself a hand of 5 cards, and it comes up, miraculously, as a Royal Flush. It's the perfect hand! A Straight, A Flush, and all face cards.

Now imagine that some mysterious God has decided that you're locked in a time maze until you can deal that hand to yourself again, blindfolded, when someone else is shuffling the deck. You can't die, you can't escape, until you manage to pull that Royal Flush all over again...

Lucky for you, you have a time traveling daughter that can help, but never too directly, for fear that the mad god will destroy everything. She knows that eventually you escape the maze, since she exists, so somehow, someway, you eventually land on the perfect shuffle that lets you re-deal that perfect hand...but she has no idea when. So...she does what she can to subtly influence the shuffle. A nudge here, a push there, hoping that the right sequence will end things so she can stop watching you and everyone she loves suffer. Every change she makes, she can look forward and see how it ends up, but only by direct observation...but she can't see every step in between, not without experiencing it directly. It's not a direct information upload, she has to actively watch it happen.

It's omniscience and omnipotence, you're right...but it's the worst kind of torture. Knowing how a story ends, but not knowing how it got from Point A to Point Z, and every time it gets to Point T it starts all over again at Point A?

Storywise, it still works. Time Travel stories almost always fall into the fallacy of 'changing' the past to effect the present, and the future...but if you exist in the future, to observe the past, than the present has ALWAYS existed in the form you see it. The events you try to change were already changed simply by you existing. What you saw, is how the world is, no matter what changes you make in the past.

I wrote an allegory recently in a Harry Potter discussion that I think fits well here:

Imagine you had a Time Turner. You wake up, and decide to go visit a friend. You spend all day there, and come home. Once home, you remember that you're out of your life saving medicine, and were supposed to pick some up at the store. Store is closed...so you use your Time Turner to go back in time to 4pm, when the store was open, to get your medicine.

At this exact moment, TWO of you exist. Version A, Version B.

Version A is at the friends house. They are past you.
Version B is at the store, picking up the medicine. This is present you.

Version A becomes Version B. Version B has always existed, even when Version A was at the friends house. Version B can never interact with Version A, because Version B would REMEMBER that, WHEN they were Version A. Since they don't, it never happened. Version B will always make it home after Version A has gone back in time, otherwise they would remember seeing Version B, when they were Version A, and experiencing the Present.

This gets much more complicated when you allow for outside observation and changes, but that only affects the person that is outside. The person inside will always be experiencing time and events as they happened within the bubble. Every loop is a closed loop simply by existing.

The green scarf: I'm not sure why this necessitates time travel. We don't know when or how Maya Prime lost her scarf.
Maybe it was sitting forgotten in storage somewhere and Himawari just went and picked it up. That could be somewhere Maya Prime put it (like Alt Maya Prime did), or it could have been taken by the corporation at some point in the distant past.

I don't think that's even necessary, though. There are countless worlds based on the one where Akira gave Maya the scarf. Presumably each of those worlds has its own Maya clone with her own copy of the same scarf. Himawari could have gotten the scarf from any of those, and I think it would still qualify as the same scarf that Sensei gave Maya Prime because those worlds share the same past.
Himawarico: My best guess is that the company is referenced in an aspirational way, rather than as something that really exists.
Possibly Himawari invented the idea of Himawarico (with her as the sole employee) because it makes her rogue actions sound more official/important, and also because it's something she wants to do for real at some point. The times when the company seems to have a real presence are all at least on the edge of unreality (happy events, reset events, TSS, etc.), so it's not clear whether Himawarico's existence is just part of the illusion.

It's also worth noting that a Himawarico could exist without it being named for Himawari. Sunflowers have a big importance in Akira's life dating back to his childhood, for reasons that still haven't been fully explained, so a "Sunflowerco" might be part of the multiverse for other reasons. (I don't think this is likely, just worth keeping in mind)
General thoughts: If Himawari really has universal time travel powers, I agree it would weaken the story. But all of her appearances (in person or as narrator) are consistent with her experiencing the story in same linear fashion that we are. I don't think anything in 0.53 contradicts this, and in fact it gave us a reasonable explanation of where she comes from that involves no time travel at all.
The wishing well is full of worlds which are periodically reset. This doesn't involve any manipulation of time, just restoring physical/mental state to an earlier snapshot. Sensei's world (Maya's wish) is unusual in how often this happens. So in World A (Sensei's world), when Ayane gets pregnant her body gets reset to its pre-pregnancy state within a few months, and she never has her child. In a World B with longer cycles, Ayane get pregnant, gives birth, and raises Himawari to the age of fifteen all before the world resets.

After those fifteen years, World A has kept resetting and so appears to be fifteen years in the past of World B. When Himawari goes from World B to World A she appears to travel back in time fifteen years, but only because that's how the objective present in each world relate to each other. She couldn't have chosen to go to any other point of time in World A. Nothing she does in World A will affect World B, because while it looks like the past of World B, it has actually moved on to a completely new cycle.
As a final thought, I don't think we should take everything Himawari said in 0.53 as gospel. There are probably things that she has been misled about herself, and there may be things she's keeping from her parents because she thinks it's for their own good.

.

spoilers.title: Complaints about the green scarf
spoilers.html:
First of all, here Sel is clearly saying that this is the original scarf she once had, not just some random replacement. And to me, this immediately creates a huge problem: it means that Himawari can travel to any point in time. In my view, this is absolutely disastrous for the story’s internal logic. I mean, Himawari can now exist simultaneously in the past, the present, and the future. That’s basically omniscience and omnipotence. Then what’s even the point of watching the livestream? With such overwhelming power, the only things she ends up doing are… delivering a scarf to accelerate Maya’s death? Sending a watermelon when amifinger == true?
But in Untitled, she seems completely powerless again, as if she has no idea what’s going to happen in the future. If you really know the future, shouldn’t you already know that Akira will successfully escape?Especially in 0.53, she’s portrayed as equally helpless, as if she’s just trying things blindly, which is the total opposite of her usual all-knowing image.Logically speaking, she should at least be aware of all the events that happened before 0.53,right ?This is such a contradiction in the setting, and such a lack of rigor. Honestly, I suspect Sel never thought this through at all, and just thought the whole “scarf closed loop” was cool.

posts.content_html_raw:
Klldarkness said:
You've fallen into the trap of thinking, from a story POV, that just because you're outside of an event, you can know it's start, it's finish, AND all the steps in between.

Akira's story is a puzzle with a million pieces. It has a defined start, but with a near infinite variation, how you get to the defined ending is impossible to full predict, even for someone that know how it's supposed to end.

Imagine, if you will, that you have a deck of cards in your hands. You deal yourself a hand of 5 cards, and it comes up, miraculously, as a Royal Flush. It's the perfect hand! A Straight, A Flush, and all face cards.

Now imagine that some mysterious God has decided that you're locked in a time maze until you can deal that hand to yourself again, blindfolded, when someone else is shuffling the deck. You can't die, you can't escape, until you manage to pull that Royal Flush all over again...

Lucky for you, you have a time traveling daughter that can help, but never too directly, for fear that the mad god will destroy everything. She knows that eventually you escape the maze, since she exists, so somehow, someway, you eventually land on the perfect shuffle that lets you re-deal that perfect hand...but she has no idea when. So...she does what she can to subtly influence the shuffle. A nudge here, a push there, hoping that the right sequence will end things so she can stop watching you and everyone she loves suffer. Every change she makes, she can look forward and see how it ends up, but only by direct observation...but she can't see every step in between, not without experiencing it directly. It's not a direct information upload, she has to actively watch it happen.

It's omniscience and omnipotence, you're right...but it's the worst kind of torture. Knowing how a story ends, but not knowing how it got from Point A to Point Z, and every time it gets to Point T it starts all over again at Point A?

Storywise, it still works. Time Travel stories almost always fall into the fallacy of 'changing' the past to effect the present, and the future...but if you exist in the future, to observe the past, than the present has ALWAYS existed in the form you see it. The events you try to change were already changed simply by you existing. What you saw, is how the world is, no matter what changes you make in the past.

I wrote an allegory recently in a Harry Potter discussion that I think fits well here:

Imagine you had a Time Turner. You wake up, and decide to go visit a friend. You spend all day there, and come home. Once home, you remember that you're out of your life saving medicine, and were supposed to pick some up at the store. Store is closed...so you use your Time Turner to go back in time to 4pm, when the store was open, to get your medicine.

At this exact moment, TWO of you exist. Version A, Version B.

Version A is at the friends house. They are past you.
Version B is at the store, picking up the medicine. This is present you.

Version A becomes Version B. Version B has always existed, even when Version A was at the friends house. Version B can never interact with Version A, because Version B would REMEMBER that, WHEN they were Version A. Since they don't, it never happened. Version B will always make it home after Version A has gone back in time, otherwise they would remember seeing Version B, when they were Version A, and experiencing the Present.

This gets much more complicated when you allow for outside observation and changes, but that only affects the person that is outside. The person inside will always be experiencing time and events as they happened within the bubble. Every loop is a closed loop simply by existing.
Click to expand...
I understand what you mean—you’re saying that Himawari doesn’t know what the future will be after she takes action. But to me, that makes it even more crazy, because everything she does is essentially a gamble. She has no idea whether her actions will make things better or worse. That’s what makes her saying “It was show time.” after getting the scarf feel somewhat ironic, because we all know what ends up happening. If Maya’s death wasn’t part of her plan, that makes her seem even more like a child who completely messed things up—so much so that by the end of 0.53, she’s severely warned, runs out of action points, can’t do anything at all, and ends up begging Shiori for help.

Alright, tech stuff and small event guide for the update.
To begin with, Sel forgot to define karinspring7miss. Just fixed, download this. The new fix includes the former.
If it doesn't have a line break, it means you need to trigger the event before it to see it.
You'll miss a few events if you missed the Kirin TSS or if you're a good uncle.

Wakana 1: Automatic at night, Wakana Affection 40+, finished Osako events from last update.
Wakana 2: Morning before Saturday, has priority over the Kirin event.

Noriko 1: Invite Noriko at 50+ Affection, this triggers Noriko 2 and Ami 1.
Kirin: Morning before Friday.
Karin: Afternoon Weekend, triggers Ami 2.
Niki 1: Morning Sunday, this triggers Niki 2, Main 1, Chinami 1, Main 2 and Chinami 2.
Nao: Ramen Wednesday.

Doesn't mean it will throw the error window, just a message of missing file. Just fixed, download this.

After Wakana 1, you get a Rika picture message.

Okay, I think that's all.

To begin with, Sel forgot to define karinspring7miss. Just fixed, download this. The new fix includes the former.
If it doesn't have a line break, it means you need to trigger the event before it to see it.
You'll miss a few events if you missed the Kirin TSS or if you're a good uncle.

Wakana 1: Automatic at night, Wakana Affection 40+, finished Osako events from last update.
Wakana 2: Morning before Saturday, has priority over the Kirin event.

Noriko 1: Invite Noriko at 50+ Affection, this triggers Noriko 2 and Ami 1.
Kirin: Morning before Friday.
Karin: Afternoon Weekend, triggers Ami 2.
Niki 1: Morning Sunday, this triggers Niki 2, Main 1, Chinami 1, Main 2 and Chinami 2.
Nao: Ramen Wednesday.

You can call Kaori at night for a blowjob too besides her usual events.

Trying to visit Maki when she's unavailable now sends you to the correct menu instead of the pre-chapter 4 one.

After Christmalloween, inviting Sana also lets you do her cowgirl. But the event is currently bugged because Sel did an oopsie in the code (and also misplaced the Sana images, I think, since they're in the events folder instead of the animations one). Doesn't mean it will throw the error window, just a message of missing file. Just fixed, download this.

After Wakana 1, you get a Rika picture message.

Okay, I think that's all.

posts.content_html_raw:
I'll just go ahead and begin my update analysis/recap right away.
This update felt both short but impactful at the same time, if that makes sense.
Some major stuff happening that was bound to take place since forever, while everything else felt more like a set-up, building blocks for things to come.
All in all, I would give this update the title "Planting the seed". Read my spoilers to understand why. Also follow, subscribe and don't forget to hit the like button.

This one is gonna be pretty straightforward, nothing too surprising here. Wakana, in a moment of weakness, has no other option but to rely on Akira and lean on his shoulder. And man does this guy have rizz, making even Wakana smile and actually pull off calming her down a little.
They do have insane chemistry. It just feels real and natural. I just love how they bounce off each other in a weirdly wholesome way. And Wakana is the goat at looking at Akira disapprovingly.
Imani is 100% correct in detecting her as her biggest romantic rival (that she knows of at least), which is ironic given that she is one of the characters furthest away from wanting to fuck him, right after Osako. And even that assumption is slowly crumbling away.

Sel has been anything but vague in his depiction of what's next to come. He underlines how she very much acknowledges his god given physical gift and even plants the seed of creating a scenario where she might get a go at him.
Obviously Rika's idea has been immediately identified as what it is, just another of her insane approaches to solve problems, but Sel wouldn't address it in this detail if it weren't to come true in one way or another during future events. As ludicrous as the idea appears at first glance, it has some shimmer of logic or at least hope in it. It's so dumb, it may work. Which is actually very similar to another event's conclusion, more on this later.

Because first, I want to express that Rika is growing on me, she is hella funny and really wholesome and helpful in a way. Like a puppy, kinda dumb and naive and causing trouble but you know her heart is in the right place and she just doesn't know better. And as TheGoodPastor said, the text messages were just the cherry on top.
At least in the variant I picked, she tells him she loves him which he, both unsurprisingly and this time probably also justifiably, feels uncalled for and insincere, in addition to making him feel uncomfortable as it is always the case for him sharing genuine feelings of love.
But unlike many other characters, she actually doubles down on it confidently, because in her mind and her understanding of what love is, she does love him and she wants him to know that (even if he doesn't understand it the same way). Cute.
Justice is served, Noriko gets her (mostly) uninterrupted sex event and it's the Noriko-typical mix of hot, cute, wholesome, crazy and hot. I just feel so happy for her and I'm not even her #1 fan on here (that title probably goes to Mr. DemonCock).

What I don't feel happy for is that I once again get punished for being on a good uncle run and that the demon spawn Ami is not only stealing away my nerves, patience and sanity whenever I see her, she even steals precious game time with other characters again and again. I assume it's just Ami x Noriko action, which I am okay with missing, but do let me know if there is anything more substantial I was forced to miss.

Which leads me to...
Moonflare, please skip the next few sentences, thanks
Kirin is being wholesome again, in her own way at least. She has fully come around to get a reality check and is embracing it. She knows what she wants, she is fully aware of how inappropriate and likely hormone driven it is, but she can't help it and is trying to deal with it in the most reasonable way she can think of. Good for her.

Even more wholesome, as per usual, is her sister. *Tim Robinson voice* She is NOT boring!
As I once said before already, she is essentially one of the most reasonable and sane characters in the game, all things considered. She mostly sees Akira for what he would look like to the average bystander (and she even only knows the half of it really), a depressive, sex-addicted, snarky but luckily handsome David Duchovny groomer who is essentially dangerous and should be approached with caution.
Now this event underlines how much of this alleged awareness contrasts with her general naivety in terms of romance, sexuality and ulterior motives. Though she is showing clear signs of growing out of it, without abandoning her principles. She understands she is in the minority with her conservative approach to life, love and sexuality, but she still wants to be taken seriously for it and for others to respect her boundaries. She is maturing, and as part of that, the thought of being with Akira and it not being necessarily inappropriate and wrong is maturing as well. The seed has been planted.
Ironically, this is exactly where she just gets taken advantage of again but the red haired trash can that is Ami.

It was nice to see Akira being angrier than I think I have ever seen him before. When he said he thinks she shouldn't live her anymore, I was about to jump in joy, but of course she managed to play on his heart strings a bit and weasel her way out of it somehow.

It's almost unnerving how Ami is dropping her facade more and more with each of her events. She feels confident enough to just lay out her cards in front of Akira, referring to all of this as a game, even straight up insulting him in his face.
I kind of just don't want to dwell on her right now anymore, she just pisses me off. And looking at my screenshots with the drugged up Karin in the background just makes me sick.

For anyone not getting the David Duchovny bit, he was a famous actor from the 90s/2000s who was basically an arrogant but handsome sex addict that cheated on his wife and was mostly an asshole in general.
This is clearly the dominant event in this update, something that was bound to happen basically since Niki was introduced. And it's a well needed catalyst to get a few things going as well.
First off, this whole event shows how much of a great organizer and people-understander Noriko is. A perfectly choregraphed plan that even an idiot like Akira could not ruin. And she even initiates it herself. Niki later calls their talk "my sister softening me up to the idea". Or in other words, planting the seed of forgiveness.

Now one thing I really didn't expect to be confronted with is Peter Gabriel. And as weirdly annoying and random as the song was, it was admittedly hilarious and in truly Sel fashion somehow ended up fitting the scene more than expected.
I'm not a lawyer, but I feel like I know enough to understand what the term "commercial use" means though. As confident as Sel might be, and as funny as it was in game, I don't really follow his logic. The terms presented prohibit commercial use of the song, and the game (or access to it) is being sold, i.e. it is a commercial product.
Now I know in the US "fair use" can be a somewhat loose and general term, but I personally just don't see it applied here.
Sure, it's unlikely the legal team of Peter Gabriel Ltd. is scouring the internet outside of YouTube and maybe Twitch and other platforms for his copyrighted music, but I don't see it entirely out of the question that someone would, just to spite his big ass ego, report its use to them in his works and given the nature of this game, I could actually imagine them taking action to not have his name associated with a game where teenagers are being groomed.

Now am I crazy or is Sel really just way too confident in his own cognitive abilities again? Or the "Lawyer" referenced was just some guy on Lilcord that he got legal counsel from? Who knows.
We know that for the story Niki has to return, she can't just avoid him forever. But she does so very unwillingly, self-aware of how incredibly dumb it is and how she should feel terrible for it, how she will regret it etc. It's a bit odd, simply because it's really unreasonable to the point where you'd want say "Really, girl? All that, just for him?". But it is addressed, she is aware of how ridiculous it is that she agrees to it. As I mentioned earlier with Wakana, this whole plan is so dumb and so unrealistic, it might work out in the end.
The narrator even mentions that no matter how unrealistic and idiotic some behavior and decision in romcoms appear, that is how love works sometimes.
And speaking of which: I might be dumb or too tired by now, but did we just get a confirmation that Kyoko is one of the narrators?
At first it felt like it was supposed to indicate that it's Nodoka, since she is at her desk and it's literally showing her. But obviously it doesn't really make sense, Nodoka is not suddenly all-knowing or a second Ami Prime. To me it feels like a bait-and-switch, that it's actually Kyoko. She is stuck at a desk as shown during Nodoka's last appearance, "slipping away" indefinitely. It would make sense if one of the narrators was her, and if that's the case, she clearly was for this part of the event, with the desk comment and showing Nodoka at the same time.
Maybe someone smarter than me can share their thoughts on this, as much as this is even relevant or interesting.
Just when I thought we were finally descending the pile of shit that was the "Chika has rabies and is being insufferable" arc, they just shovel heaps and heaps of dung on it again. Give me a break with this girl.
We know it had to happen, for this particular scenario it feels like it came a bit too late in Chika's already over-stretched character arc though. It makes sense that she would somewhat break as a result to that news, but we were also supposed to believe she was mostly over him and into Rin instead, generally just accepting her fate and positioning herself anew.
I guess she is still vulnerable and insecure enough to just be hit hard with this development, but man, like a year or two ago I imagined the reveal of Niki really being Akira's childhood friend to be much more funny and generally a comedic scene, rather than resulting in...this scary and traumatic psychosis.

The saddest part was seeing Chinami though. I feel like Chapter 1-2 Chika would bitch slap current Chika to unconsciousness and insult her in Tagalog if she found out how she basically abandons poor Chinami and scares her to bits. Not cool.
Nao later says (through Chinami) that sometimes your own mental wellbeing can be more important than others, even family (and also that Capitalism is just a means to an end and ultimately unavoidable, whether you like it or not, maybe the most politically sane sentence Sel has ever blurted out). While I would definitely agree to that, I don't feel like it applies here though. Chika is just being a bitch again, mostly. But I guess Nao knows best.

One thing we learned recently is how good Sel is at writing extremely creepy groomers and how authentic they feel in the way they talk, courtesy of the Haruka event with Kirin. That shit was gross.
Similarly, to me, the whole vibe with the anthropomorphic animal party goers was really off. I feel like most of us know people like that or have been in contact with such people at some point.
In any case, it was remarkable how nuanced and subtle their predatory behavior was showcased and how believably unaware of it someone like Chinami would be. Also, again, a nice touch with the panther, an apex predator, being the most concerned with her, while the hare of all the animal guests was the most straightforward one. Also I'm an idiot and always thought hares were male rabbits, fuck me I guess.

Are they really intending to "fix" this "doomed world" or are they basically just like the gods that Himawari mentioned who watch it as a form of entertainment?

Considering the bigger picture, especially with the recent updates, it's obvious that everything is revolving around Akira sexing all of the characters.
This information has been confirmed since forever, I guess mostly for content reasons though (after all this is a porn game, something I happen to forget sometimes, and people want to know if they can jack it off to their favorite waifu at some point).

Everyone, even including Nao herself, is hellbent on the mission of Akira fucking all the girls.

The idea that achieving consensual sex (aka green path) leads you to the true end, while having to force one or several characters to do it to get to the end content would lock you out of the true end because you created more trauma as a result of you being a baby-back bitch (aka choosing any red path).

Anyways, I'm eager to read other posts covering this event to shed some more light on its possible meaning and consequences.

This update felt both short but impactful at the same time, if that makes sense.
Some major stuff happening that was bound to take place since forever, while everything else felt more like a set-up, building blocks for things to come.
All in all, I would give this update the title "Planting the seed". Read my spoilers to understand why.
Also follow, subscribe and don't forget to hit the like button.
Spoiler:
Wakana
This one is gonna be pretty straightforward, nothing too surprising here. Wakana, in a moment of weakness, has no other option but to rely on Akira and lean on his shoulder. And man does this guy have rizz, making even Wakana smile and actually pull off calming her down a little.

Spoiler
Imani is 100% correct in detecting her as her biggest romantic rival (that she knows of at least), which is ironic given that she is one of the characters furthest away from wanting to fuck him, right after Osako. And even that assumption is slowly crumbling away.

does
love him and she wants him to know that (even if he doesn't understand it the same way). Cute.
Spoiler

groomer who is essentially dangerous and should be approached with caution.

And she even initiates it herself. Niki later calls their talk "my sister softening me up to the idea". Or in other words, planting the seed of forgiveness.
Now one thing I really didn't expect to be confronted with is Peter Gabriel. And as weirdly annoying and random as the song was, it was admittedly hilarious and in truly Sel fashion somehow ended up fitting the scene more than expected.
Spoiler:
legal rant
I'm not a lawyer, but I feel like I know enough to understand what the term "commercial use" means though. As confident as Sel might be, and as funny as it was in game, I don't really follow his logic. The terms presented prohibit commercial use of the song, and the game (or access to it) is being sold, i.e. it is a commercial product.
Now I know in the US "fair use" can be a somewhat loose and general term, but I personally just don't see it applied here.
Sure, it's unlikely the legal team of Peter Gabriel Ltd. is scouring the internet outside of YouTube and maybe Twitch and other platforms for his copyrighted music, but I don't see it entirely out of the question that someone would, just to spite his big ass ego, report its use to them in his works and given the nature of this game, I could actually imagine them taking action to not have his name associated with a game where teenagers are being groomed.
Now am I crazy or is Sel really just way too confident in his own cognitive abilities again? Or the "Lawyer" referenced was just some guy on Lilcord that he got legal counsel from? Who knows.
We know that for the story Niki
has
to return, she can't just avoid him forever. But she does so very unwillingly, self-aware of how incredibly dumb it is and how she should feel terrible for it, how she will regret it etc. It's a bit odd, simply because it's really unreasonable to the point where you'd want say "Really, girl? All that, just for
him
?". But it
is
addressed, she
is
aware of how ridiculous it is that she agrees to it. As I mentioned earlier with Wakana, this whole plan is so dumb and so unrealistic, it might work out in the end.
The narrator even mentions that no matter how unrealistic and idiotic some behavior and decision in romcoms appear, that
is
how love works sometimes.
And speaking of which: I might be dumb or too tired by now, but did we just get a confirmation that Kyoko is one of the narrators?
Spoiler
At first it felt like it was supposed to indicate that it's Nodoka, since she is at her desk and it's literally showing her. But obviously it doesn't really make sense, Nodoka is not suddenly all-knowing or a second Ami Prime. To me it feels like a bait-and-switch, that it's actually Kyoko. She is stuck at a desk as shown during Nodoka's last appearance, "slipping away" indefinitely. It would make sense if one of the narrators was her, and if that's the case, she clearly was for this part of the event, with the desk comment
and
showing Nodoka at the same time.
Maybe someone smarter than me can share their thoughts on this, as much as this is even relevant or interesting.

spoilers.title: Chika & Chinami
spoilers.html:
Just when I thought we were finally descending the pile of shit that was the "Chika has rabies and is being insufferable" arc, they just shovel heaps and heaps of dung on it again. Give me a break with this girl.
We know it had to happen, for this particular scenario it feels like it came a bit too late in Chika's already over-stretched character arc though. It makes sense that she would somewhat break as a result to that news, but we were also supposed to believe she was mostly over him and into Rin instead, generally just accepting her fate and positioning herself anew.
I guess she is still vulnerable and insecure enough to just be hit hard with this development, but man, like a year or two ago I imagined the reveal of Niki really being Akira's childhood friend to be much more funny and generally a comedic scene, rather than resulting in...this scary and traumatic psychosis.

The saddest part was seeing Chinami though. I feel like Chapter 1-2 Chika would bitch slap current Chika to unconsciousness and insult her in Tagalog if she found out how she basically abandons poor Chinami and scares her to bits. Not cool.
Nao later says (through Chinami) that sometimes your own mental wellbeing can be more important than others, even family (and also that Capitalism is just a means to an end and ultimately unavoidable, whether you like it or not, maybe the most politically sane sentence Sel has ever blurted out). While I would definitely agree to that, I don't feel like it applies here though. Chika is just being a bitch again, mostly. But I guess Nao knows best.

One thing we learned recently is how good Sel is at writing extremely creepy groomers and how authentic they feel in the way they talk, courtesy of the Haruka event with Kirin. That shit was gross.
Similarly, to me, the whole vibe with the anthropomorphic animal party goers was really off. I feel like most of us know people like that or have been in contact with such people at some point.
In any case, it was remarkable how nuanced and subtle their predatory behavior was showcased and how believably unaware of it someone like Chinami would be. Also, again, a nice touch with the panther, an apex predator, being the most concerned with her, while the hare of all the animal guests was the most straightforward one. Also I'm an idiot and always thought hares were male rabbits, fuck me I guess.
The whole heroin joke was also very good, honestly, this whole segment was just really clever writing. I hate to do it, but I have to toot Sel's horn from time to time when it's deserved.

However, who the fuck was Chinami throwing under the bus with this line?
She basically only knows Yumi and Akira, right? Maybe Touka I guess. I mean, Akira is kinda lame and weird, but I feel like Chinami doesn't see him that way at all. And Yumi would straight up beat her ass if she was to find out she called her lame and weird. I feel like I'm forgetting someone or an event that this would be a reference to.

In any case, as off-putting as it was to watch this ordeal, the purpose was very clear. Chinami is now more curious than ever, she now believes kissing someone you like as a friend is fine and she needs to learn that stuff anyway.
Big time seed planting happening right there.

spoilers.title: wtf was that Nao event
spoilers.html:
Now this is definitely more so territory for aramaug, Moonflare and the likes. I feel like this was a bit too deep for me.

Who the fuck was the narrator and why is Nao able to interact with them directly? Kaori has been rumored to be a narrator, would this be another hint at that? They call her "My Daughter" at the end. Idk.

Why is Ami being shown (twice) in relation to the lake from Terminal 22?
Why are Amiokay and Moyo trying to force Nao to talk?
Are they really intending to "fix" this "doomed world" or are they basically just like the gods that Himawari mentioned who watch it as a form of entertainment?

Also, since when did Nao actively want to sex Akira? Was it ever referenced before? (Not counting her somewhat willingly watching him fuck)

Considering the bigger picture, especially with the recent updates, it's obvious that everything is revolving around Akira sexing all of the characters.
This information has been confirmed since forever, I guess mostly for content reasons though (after all this is a porn game, something I happen to forget sometimes, and people want to know if they can jack it off to their favorite waifu at some point).
But why, canonically speaking, is that the case?

Everyone, even including Nao herself, is hellbent on the mission of Akira fucking all the girls.
And what does it mean for the red path playthroughs?
I don't see a scenario where it will be possible to ignore the fact that for some players this will be unachievable, unless there will be specific events that make Akira sex all those optional characters. But then that would make the green path not green anymore? That just seems very unlikely.
Though I would not be opposed to it. The idea that achieving consensual sex (aka green path) leads you to the true end, while having to force one or several characters to do it to get to the end content would lock you out of the true end because you created more trauma as a result of you being a baby-back bitch (aka choosing any red path).

Otherwise it would just mean that any red path must result in an early game over while only the green path enables the end content. And that would feel lame.

Anyways, I'm eager to read other posts covering this event to shed some more light on its possible meaning and consequences.
