posts.content_html_raw:
Pretty serviceable update overall. A shame it was shorter than usual, but what we got was mostly good.

Okay, let’s get into it.

Poor Wakana… It’s true that sometimes all it takes is one major disagreement to unravel everything. I know this has to happen in order for Wakana and Osako both to eventually wind up with Akira, but still. It’s a shame. I like them both a lot and was rooting for their relationship. A threesome with them later would still be really hot.
Good to see Noriko getting some more action. She’s becoming more active to get what she wants, and I like that. The sex scene with Ami was pretty hot all things considered.

Does the fact Noriko came so hard when she was forced to watch and touch herself mean she was more into incest than we know? Perhaps she’s into being cucked after getting used to it for so long? Or perhaps a mix of both?

I’m also glad Noriko and Niki could finally talk about what happened, as well as her helping Akira out with his apology. Things won’t ever be the same between them, but maybe this opens some other doors.
The standout events of the update for me personally. The song choice was fine. Not my favorite ever. But I did like the reference to cheesy 80’s rom-coms and how Niki’s a sucker for them lol.

Still really sucks to see Niki settle for lesser than what she wants, but considering her and Akira have a huge codependency on each other, her return was always inevitable.

I hope it can work out between them in whatever fucked up way it can. And at the very least, at the end of the tunnel, the life Niki always dreamed of will be waiting in the Purity Routes.

Also holy shit, she really just announced her relationship to the entire internet! I really can’t wait to see more of the fallout of this chaos.
Yeah I dunno man… I’m over her crazy arc too. Have been for awhile. I still feel for Chika, of course. I miss who she once was, and hope she can snap out of it and improve one day. But I just don’t see that happening anytime soon.

Sucks to see Chinami affected by it too. I’d really like to see Yumi take on a more active role again in Chinami’s care, because clearly she knows Chika’s off her rocker. And we know Akira won’t do shit. So honestly, Yumi is her best bet. Maybe even Noriko can help? Or Osako meets her somehow?

Considering Osako wants children of her own, and she’s been trying new hobbies for herself, I could see her trying a temp job as a babysitter and having to watch Chinami and maybe Tsukasa too for some experience. That’d be fun to witness. And chaotic.
First of all, thank you for destroying that old dude’s phone, Kirin. I don’t blame you in the slightest.

Secondly, I’m really proud of Kirin for working on herself. I really am. Others may not agree, and it certainly doesn’t wash away her past sins at all, but y’know what? At least she’s trying to be better. She apologized to Karin for her behavior which was long overdue.

Of course, Kirin goes on to confess her love for Akira immediately after, and things do get argumentative again, but that’s to be expected. As Kirin said, Karin has her own problems to sort through as well. It’s a tough situation all around.

I hope Kirin continues down her path of bettering herself one step at a time. I love to see it.
It’s so completely and utterly fucked up what happened to her. Kirin warned Karin about her being too trusting being potentially dangerous, and what happened? She trusted Ami and got drugged for it.

When I saw her tied up in Akira’s room with Ami presenting her like some sort of prize, I about lost my damn mind. I feared Akira would once again be manipulated by Ami, because that’s just what always happens.

I was pleading deep down for Akira to do the right thing, the bare minimum, for once. And to his credit, he actually did and then some.

I don’t think I’ve ever seen Akira so pissed off. It was a bit jarring, but so satisfying when he told Ami to get the fuck out. Now true, you can say that threats mean nothing without action, but the fact Akira gave Ami an ultimatum at all and didn’t fold to her demands at least shows that he’s finally done with her shit.

It feels so satisfying to see after so many updates of him giving her the benefit of the doubt.

Speaking of which…
Fuck, man. What can I say about Ami at this point? She just sucks lol. At least, this Imposter Ami does. Yeah that’s right, I’m still huffing that copium. And I’ll keep huffing until I’m proven otherwise.

At the very least, you can’t say her villainy doesn’t make things interesting. Still sooo many unanswered questions about her, but the curtain is slowly unraveling…

Can’t wait to see whose life she makes a little bit worse next update!
I’m not gonna go too into detail on this one, but a couple of things:

Wow, that TSS event was wonderfully written. It really encapsulates the mindset of a predator extremely well. Sel has always been good at writing that, while still maintaining the seriousness the subject deserves.

But wait, Nao was the Hare the whole time and even kissed Chinami?? Wtf.

I… didn’t know I needed to see them kiss, but now am glad they have.

Side characters getting TSS events opens a looot of potentially interesting possibilities. I think Niki could really use one.
Nah but seriously, though, what’s up with Nao??

Why is she always present in these TSS events? What’s her goal? Why try to help Maya? Why kiss Chinami like that?

So many questions and so little answers…

Clearly she wants Chinami to get used to the concept of trying new things, including sexual ones, but… I still wonder why.

Because she wants Akira to be happy? Because she wants to do something to the world somehow? I don’t know.

Not even gonna try to delve into that final Nao event. It was just strange and I don’t know what to even make of it.

So I’ll leave that to the deep thinkers of the forum.

But yeah, like I said, solid update overall. Nothing too disturbing this time, so that’s a plus. Have to wonder where the next update will take us before the second Fanfest.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just to address the hare incident:
I don't think the hare was supposed to have been Nao-chan the whole time. I'm pretty certain she just brought back Chinami just in time before she actually got to kiss the hare, ending up kissing her herself. And being this otherworldly, sex-positive entity, she just went ahead and enjoyed it? I imagine from the hare's perspective, she just kinda popped out of existence in their dimension (much like a certain someone's million-year-old ex-lover).

As I mentioned in my post, Nao is clearly dead-set on getting every girl to accept that it's okay to let Akira bonk them (see her, I guess, helping deal with Io's trauma with her Mom in the last update) and this is an especially straightforward attempt.

Also one thing regarding the Niki event:
Since I've seen it addressed already:
Sel is walking a fine line in my opinion with having Akira just be able to come up with an excuse to lure girls into his harem by vaguely stating "Well you see, I have this undescriptive feeling in the back of my head, like a forgotten dream, that somehow I will be able to manufacture a purity route for every single one of you, a world in which we will live happily ever after, so just stick with me through the dark route and you will not regret it, based on nothing at all. Trust".
I don't know, that logic seemed awfully wobbly.
Akira does not remember this "dream" (which is btw I believe what Ami was referring to in this update*), however he can still understand the conclusions that came out of it?
He is telling Ami that he knows he is missing something, clearly referring to his new-found desire to become a father, and to Niki he is explaining his unshattered belief that he will get to have a happy end with each character (referencing Himawari's wish worlds, aka purity routes).
It does feel a bit too convenient for this to be enough to drive things forward. Intrinsically, sure, I guess he can find this motivation within himself emerging simply from a subconscious feeling, a deeply planted seed by Himawari. But why would others simply believe his words when he himself does not understand where it comes from?

I hope this whole story arc will unravel more smoothly going forward and not end up feeling like lazy writing.

*which, if true, would also mean that Ami is aware of Himawari's plan, possibly having watched them or learned of what she told Akira and Ayane.

As a fellow staunch Ami defender, I believe that this interpretation of her actions in 0.56 is mostly correct, because we know that she has been insistently pushing on treating everything that happens in Kumon-mi as a videogame from the very-very beginning: from Ami eagerly taking up the role of the obligatory “info-dumping NPC for the new players” in “A New You” (despite, presumably, being fully aware of what is *actually* happening, in addition to having likely already done this routine countless times with all of Sensei’s previous “iterations”), to the stuff she says to Sensei in the middle her mental breakdown in “Della”:

“Nothing makes sense here! It’s not supposed to! You’re supposed to treat this like a game! You’re supposed to get me pregnant! You’re supposed to reach the epilogue!”

Add to that the fact that Ami has been repeatedly referring to herself as “the main heroine” over the course of all four Chapters thus far (or the protagonist of the entire story, *period*, going by one of her lines in "A Vivid Explosion of Color"), as well as Sensei (effectively being forced into) pledging to “only play the Ami route” in “Friends (The Maya Route)”, Ami’s behavior during this update actually makes perfect sense and is fully logically consistent:

She wants Akira to “reach the epilogue” – which, since this is an H-game, inevitably necessitates him “fully completing the CG gallery” by “romancing” all of the available characters. However, the guy has been stuck in his depression phase for the third year in a row at this point, with no clear end in sight, and that is without even mentioning him “regressing back to having morals” (as insanely nonsensical and hypocritical they are in this particular case), so Ami feels like she has no choice but to take matters in her own hands and accelerate the process of “rounding out the collection” by quite literally bringing him the girls on a silver platter. In some cases, it means subtly playing matchmaker (like her saying that “it would be nice to have someone like you around our house” and “I think the two of you would make a great couple” to Wakana in “From the Horse’s Mouth”), while in others it means directly orchestrating the events in such a way where they are likely to result in sex with one of the yet-unfucked females (like what Ami did to Noriko in 0.50 – which was *also* a “two birds with one stone” situation, since it served a second purpose of helping her get rid of Niki – or to Karin here).

So, yeah, Ami best girl. I *cannot wait* to see how her role as (seemingly) the main antagonist at this current point in the story is going to be expanded upon in the future updates, considering that there is basically *no way* that Ami is *just* going to be an obstacle for Akira/Niki to overcome (plus, by Selebus’ own admission, she is the character that we still probably understand the least about, aside from maybe Nao-chan), so I’m expecting some next-level twists and turns in regards to our favorite incest gremlin.

posts.content_html_raw:
DeanNoriko said:
Now this is definitely more so territory for aramaug, Moonflare and the likes. I feel like this was a bit too deep for me.

Who the fuck was the narrator and why is Nao able to interact with them directly? Kaori has been rumored to be a narrator, would this be another hint at that? They call her "My Daughter" at the end. Idk.

Why is Ami being shown (twice) in relation to the lake from Terminal 22?
Why are Amiokay and Moyo trying to force Nao to talk?
Are they really intending to "fix" this "doomed world" or are they basically just like the gods that Himawari mentioned who watch it as a form of entertainment?

Also, since when did Nao actively want to sex Akira? Was it ever referenced before? (Not counting her somewhat willingly watching him fuck)

[...]

Anyways, I'm eager to read other posts covering this event to shed some more light on its possible meaning and consequences.
Click to expand...
While I obviously don’t have any 100% concrete or confirmed answers (this was an incredibly weird event, even by LiL’s standards – and, like someone mentioned earlier, it had the feeling of being “artistically unfinished”) here are some notable things and observations that I managed to make while reading (and then re-reading) “Menma”:

1. First of all, it is somewhat likely that the entire event has been a dream sequence of some kind and not actually physically happening in reality, in the similar vein as “Second Sun”:

– For one, everything that occurs in “Menma” very much *feels* like something you’d see in a dream with how out of nowhere, disjointed and nonsensical the whole premise is: Sensei randomly coming to Tojo Ramen while behaving like a total lunatic, only to find that Nao-chan is also there for some reason – notably alone, without Kaori – and Tsuneyo is very conveniently “absent/on break/put in the corner”. Additionally, it just in general feels like a complete narrative non-sequitur, since there was no prior set-up to this event, it wasn’t foreshadowed in any way, *and* it has no tie-ins with any other currently developing plotlines, which was the case for all of previous Nao-chan’s events in Chapter 4 (everything up to 0.45 connects to the USERs, Kaori and/or Pareidolia; “Wings of Anhedonia” connects to Yumi and Yuki’s situation, plus references “Sonny Boy and The Magnificent Waiting Room”; “Miracle” connects to Sekaori, Wakana/Osako relationship and Resets as a whole; and “Nao More Than Ever” connects to Maya and her trying to figure out her place in this world).

– There are also multiple references to “dreams” or “dreaming” during the event itself, like the Great Overlook being described as “unlike a dream, but not unlike a dream too”, Akira “dreaming of a lake” or the mysterious narrator saying “sleep, girl; dream, girl; be, girl” to Nao-chan near the end of it.

– Finally, the ending of the event – as I interpreted it, anyway – appears to be Nao-chan intentionally replicating a very specific position close to Sensei, falling asleep and then waking up in the real world in the exact same position (maybe in Tojo Ramen, maybe in some other place – I can’t determine this for sure), potentially implying that they’ve both been dreaming this whole time, and the pose Nao-chan takes (with Sensei holding her closely) is the one they originally fell asleep in.

2. Speaking of the mysterious narrator, I have a strong suspicion that the one narrating “Menma” is Nao – as in, the Xoanon, the one presiding over the Great Library. Their personality: clearly ascendent and enlightened, but also intentionally cryptic, in addition to being very unsubtly condescending towards “lesser beings” – strongly lines up with how Nao spoke to Sensei in “Mother’s Milk”, and it also somewhat explains the “my daughter” connection, since the mystery of why Nao-chan shares a name with one of the highest-level meta-entities we’ve seen in the game has been completely ignored by the story thus far.

3. During her “God is a staircase” metaphor, Youdidit refers to Nao-chan as “an incomplete butterfly” – a reference that is much more meaningful that it might initially appear, because one of the characters in “Sonny Boy & The Magnificent Waiting Room” is called Incomplete Butterfly (he points to an incomplete picture and asks “Something should go here. What do you think it is?”, the correct answer to which is “9”), and we know from “What's in the Pot?” that Nao-chan’s “internal system handle” is TEMPLATE9, and she is also directly connected to USER4.

4. USER4 might also be “Him” mentioned by the narrator near the end of the event (due to all of the aforementioned reasons) – or, alternatively, it could be HOPE, since Youdidit/Moyo *are* presumably still employed by him, fitting in with the very HOPE-like line

“SUCK IT, YOU MYSTERIOUS GIRL-WHORE! LET THE SCALES OF WISDOM REPLACE YOUR UNMOVING TONGUE WITH A TAPEWORM BOUND TO VERBALITY!”

Youdidit says to Nao-chan while pushing the “fish” into her mouth, and the fact that the symbols of both “tongue” and “worm” *are* generally associated with HOPE the most among the Trinity.

5. As for the symbology of the fish itself, I genuinely have no fucking idea. The only thing that immediately comes to my mind upon hearing “the fish of wisdom” is the Irish legend of Fionn mac Cumhaill – it was the Salmon of Knowledge there, specifically – but, like, I don’t know how else to connect Fionn’s mythos to Nao-chan, so this is probably a thematical dead end and has nothing to do with Selebus’ intention regarding “Menma”.

6. Finally, to briefly touch upon some of the other questions you brought up (that haven’t been covered by my earlier observations):

– Ami being shown in relation to Terminal 22 is seemingly a part of Sensei’s “dream” he is having in this event, and could thus be one of two things: either a symbolic manifestation of his troubles with Ami in the entire 0.56 update, as she effectively “injects herself” into this dream like she “injects herself” into all aspects of his life as a whole – or, alternatively, an implication that Sensei dreaming about his parents/family eventually transforms into him beginning to dream about Ami, since the house on the lake *did* belong to Ami’s grandmother, and they *did* use to live there for at least *some* time, as confirmed by the girl herself in “Goodnight Moon”.

– Nao-chan being sexually interested in Akira has been explicitly confirmed ever since “Miracle”, where she outright writes so as one of her responses to Osako, and could have been potentially implied even as early as “Kittens”.

I am, for once, not going to talk shit about Ami despite how much I dislike her, but unlike some people who defend her (what the fuck) I won't try to justify her actions as I don't think there is enough information to go on just yet - at least for something concrete other than theories - but I do want to say I appreciate her character for what she is now.

I think Selly has done a pretty good job with her character and how she is presented to us the players/readers and her interactions with the rest of the cast. The way she has evolved from the sweet girl with incestuous cravings to this actual degenerate is so interesting and entertaining, in a way that gives the whole story more depth, IMO. She is not just part of the story, she is taking over or at least letting us know she is way more involved AND in control than previously thought, something about how confident she is and this "I don't give a shit about your feelings" attitude while still having her own insecurities and doubts; I love it.

And I know there are some theories about this not being the real Ami, I would personally hate this being the case because that would take away a lot from the character and their story as a whole. So yeah, while she is easy to hate to some extent and won't even try to defend her actions (again what the fuck) I still love her character and I'm glad she exists for the little demon she is.

Also that "Sips incestuously" was so funny.

I am only joking on her defenders, don't mean no offense. Even if it's questionable.

Overall I thought the update was good! A bit shorter and not quite at the level of the previous several but good nonetheless.

It felt tonally a bit inconsistent but that might be mitigated in a full game playthrough as the events themselves were all great.

Wakana - In full on denial despite Imani's pinpoint accuracy with her Akira love detector. Her rare Goth Smile could melt mountains. Its really sad to see her and Osako in the doldrums but it doesn't seem insurmountable. There's gotta be some path forward for them via Lesbian magic. Maybe it serves as a catalyst to a second foursome/boner time, which has a great track record for Akira fixing things.

Noriko - Ahh yeah lets go. Great dialogue in the invite and then the Ami surprise was fantastic. Noriko once again showing shes at least A tier with her setting up the Niki reunion. Good work Noriko, you get one Akira shaped gold star.

Niki - Great reunion and reasoning to get Niki back. I wanted more hate sex personally but the social media bomb is a good substitute. I like how the utter insanity and stupidity of their relationship is lampshaded, then used to reinforce why they belong together. The exact pain to good ratio may be way off, but neither can long resist the other. The Harem has one more fully aware and accepting member. Its always better with a super tsundere Idol then not.

Maya - Poor girl did not need to catch that stray. Poor Maya.

Kirin - I'm a card carrying member of the Kirin redemption committee and I'm not ashamed. Despicable crimes? Crass behavior? Formerly unapologetic general awfulness? All there and accounted for. She's actively trying and being honest now. Theres a long road ahead and a ton of apologies to make and be accepted, but I believe in our sis-con. Kirin just needed a lesson in love to turn it all around.

Karin - Poor unsuspecting Karin. She keeps opening her heart and trusting the worst of people. But at the same time, Ami WTF.

Karins just a good girl who wants the best for her sister. She's one of the few who still has a working "normal" state of mind when it comes to Akira. Her heart to heart with Kirin was wonderful.

Ami - Goddammit you incestuous little cum goblin.

You were great with Noriko, I loved seeing the casual mask off moments, and look at this you're having a nice cup of tea with a troubled girl. O lol you drink that tea incestuously girl. O how wonderful you're being a good friend and o fuck now you've drugged her.

In what world did you think that was going to work? This a newly motivated Akira, his rapes are only statutory.

Maybe it was really just to create another confrontation? She seemed really into it this time. I thought for sure she was gonna go stabby stabby when she got real close to Akira.

The direct implication of Akira trying to, in so many words, "Find his daughter" might have some serious consequences down the road. Ami might have suspected Akira's knowledge of Himawari, but this might outright confirm his lingering memory to her. Who knows what the hell Ami will do with that info.

The mask off Ami vs Akira is some of the most compelling stuff right now. I want more.

Chika - It was a little funny seeing the full Niki mind break, but I think we've had enough crazy Chika. Even with all her nonsense it felt like a Flanderization of sorts. I think the long built up payoff for her blindness when it comes to Niki was mitigated a bit by the recent Rin rabies.

Chinami - Once again we get a skin shivering rendition of a grooming. He's really good at writing those. The "prey being the predators' was a bit on the nose but effective.

So was the whole thing Nao's attempt to "marinate Chinami" for Akira's eventual sake? The event name and Nao's final actions seem to imply such. This would make Nao, Ami, and Tsubasa all acting in similar fashion to the same goal of Akira fucking everyone. Why is it so important that Akira fuck everyone? Does it again tie back to the "light" Yasu keeps talking about? Will Akira provide protection via unprotected penetration? IDK yet at this point.

But yeah, overall p good update. I liked it!

posts.content_html_raw:
Just gonna add this little fact here:

In Hinduism, Maya (माया) means "illusion" or "magic," a powerful cosmic force that makes the singular reality (Brahman) appear as the diverse, changing world, veiling the true, unified nature of existence. It's the creative power that projects the universe as a manifestation, leading individuals to mistake the temporary physical world, body, and ego for ultimate reality, causing attachment and suffering, though it's also seen as a divine play or power of the Goddess. Maya is the divine power that creates the cosmic illusion of a multifaceted, material world from the one ultimate reality (Brahman).

  • On a personal level, Maya manifests as avidya (ignorance), where the soul (Atman) forgets its true divine nature and identifies with the limited body and ego.
    • Concealer of Truth:
      It hides the spiritual reality, making the impermanent world seem permanent and real, leading to desires, attachments, and a cycle of birth and death (samsara).
    • Creative Power:
      Maya isn't just nothingness; it's a creative force, often equated with Prakriti (material nature) or the power of the Divine Mother (Durga/Lakshmi).
    • Overcoming Maya:
      Spiritual practices aim to transcend Maya to realize the unity of Atman and Brahman (moksha or liberation).
Examples of Maya:
    • The Wave & Ocean: A wave appears separate, but it's just the ocean's manifestation; remove the ocean, and there's no wave.
    • The Ring & Gold: A ring seems real, but it's just gold; the gold is the underlying reality.
    • Dreams & Waking Life: Like a dream, the world feels real while we're in it, but upon waking (enlightenment), its true nature is seen.
Overcoming Maya:
    • Through knowledge (vidya), devotion (bhakti), and selfless action (karma yoga), one can break free from Maya's grip.
    • The Bhagavad Gita advises transcending the gunas (modes of material nature) that form Maya.
    • Realizing the self is identical with the divine (Brahman) ends the illusion.





Also the name of Buddha's Mother is Maya.

Oh right! Before I forget:

During the Green path Ami/Noriko scene, it ends on a rather interesting sentence.

"Is this my daughter?"

Now, under normal circumstances, I'd say that there are no hidden meanings here. It's been long wondered if Ami is actually his daughter, it's mentioned in game a few times, in the multiverse reset she WAS his daughter.

But Akira isn't sure, and from what I remember, he even had a conversation about it with one of the other adults(Sara maybe? Maybe Maki?), and he straight up says he doesn't care, she's his daughter now regardless.

BUT there is also the question in the community on if the Ami we see at the start of the game is the same Ami we have now. It's possible that Original Ami popped like Maya, and was replaced with Multiverse Ami at some point during one of the resets.

During the Christmalloween reset, Akira learns that Ami certainly knows more than she lets on, but, he continues on in ignorant bliss. But it's clear he's questioning, and wondering, now, if Ami actually does know more than she is letting on.

So, finally, at last...

Do we think Akira was asking:

Is Ami ACTUALLY my daughter?

Or

Is this MY Ami?

I'm leaning towards the first, personally, because it's more likely to not be that deep...but I'm wondering what everyone else thinks on the implications.
